Subsequently, the company redomiciled back to India in March 2026 after receiving the nod from the Indian government. A month later, reports surfaced that the ecommerce major was exploring raising a pre-IPO round of $2 Bn to $2.5 Bn from Indian and foreign investors. Taking a sharp U-Turn in May 2026, reports surfaced that Flipkart had deferred its IPO till at least 2028 to focus on profitability before its public listing. This came after parent Walmart directed the ecommerce company to focus on achieving EBITDA breakeven in FY27 itself. The ecommerce major’s B2C arm, Flipkart Internet Private Ltd, reported an operating revenue of ₹20,493 Cr in FY25, up from ₹17,907 Cr in FY24. Meanwhile, losses also narrowed 37% to ₹1,494 Cr from ₹2,359 Cr, showing improved unit economics despite diversification. Furlenco Founded in 2012 by Ajith Mohan Karimpana, Furlenco operates a furniture and appliance rental platform across 28 cities like Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Chennai, and Kolkata. With over 300 SKUs, the platform also sells new furniture. Backed by Sheela Foam, Lightbox Ventures, Crescent Ventures, and White Oak, Furlenco has raised more than $290 Mn to date. In September 2026, reports surfaced that the furniture and appliance rental startup had kicked off proceedings for a potential ₹1,000-1,200 Cr public issue . Furlenco is said to be close to appointing ICICI Securities as an advisor for its IPO, which will target a valuation of around ₹7,000 Cr. Furlenco is looking to launch the IPO in FY28. The furniture rental startup turned profitable in FY25, with a net profit of ₹3.1 Cr as against a net loss of ₹130.2 Cr in FY24. Meanwhile, its revenue from operations spiked 64% to ₹228.7 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹139.6 Cr in FY24. GoBoult Founded in 2017 by Varun Gupta and Tarun Gupta, GoBoult (formerly Boult) is a smart wearables brand that sells a range of earbuds, smartwatches, neckbands and speakers. The company rebranded to a new name in August 2025 following a trademark infringement case filed by its rival boAt. The bootstrapped startup competes with the likes of boAt, Noise and Pebble. GoBoult sells its products via its own website, online marketplaces, quick commerce platforms as well as 3,000 offline stores across India. Kicking off its IPO plans, GoBoult cofounder Varun Gupta told Inc42 that the smart wearables brand is planning to file its DRHP with SEBI by November 2026. The company is eyeing a listing on the bourses by the summer of 2027. On the financial front, GoBoult reported an operating revenue of ₹762.9 Cr in FY25, up 9.4% from ₹697.2 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Its profit stood at ₹24.2 Cr during the fiscal, a near 10X jump from ₹2.5 Cr reported in FY24. Imarticus Learning Founded in 2012 by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Imarticus Learning is an edtech platform that offers upskilling programs in finance, digital marketing, data analytics, GenAI, and others to individual learners and corporate employees. The platform claims to have trained nearly 40,000 learners across B2C and B2B verticals. Backed by Global Ivy Ventures, Capian, and BLinC Invest, Imarticus has raised over $11.7 Mn to date. In April 2025, cofounder and CEO Barshikar told Inc42 the company was looking to file its DRHP with SEBI for an ₹750 Cr IPO, which would comprise both fresh issue of shares and an OFS. However, there appears to be no clarity on this front so far. While the company is yet to finalise its valuation for the IPO, bankers are said to have pitched a 25X to 30X revenue multiple for its valuation. Considering Barshikar’s claim of ₹205 Cr revenue in FY25, the edtech company could be staring at a valuation of ₹5,000 Cr to ₹6,000 Cr. Ahead of the IPO in August 2026, the edtech startup acquired Singapore-based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning for ₹800 Cr. On the financial front, Imarticus Learning’s revenue grew over 16% to ₹159 Cr in FY24 from ₹136.8 Cr in FY23, as per Tofler. Net losses, however, shot up nearly 10% to ₹24.6 Cr from ₹22.4 Cr in the year ago fiscal. InMobi Founded in 2007 by Naveen Tewari, Piyush Shah, Mohit Saxena and Abhay Singhal, InMobi is an adtech platform that offers a suite of product discovery and monetisation tools. Based in Singapore, the SaaS company also maintains offices in Bengaluru, New York, Beijing, and Dubai. With investments from Sherpalo Ventures, SoftBank, Kleiner Perkins, and others, InMobi has secured over $320 Mn in funding to date and was one of India’s earliest unicorns back in 2011. Last heard, the startup was planning to file its DRHP with SEBI for a potential $1 Bn listing at a valuation of $8 Bn to $10 Bn. In July 2026, reports surfaced that the adtech unicorn had roped in four merchant bankers , namely JPMorgan Chase, Jefferies, Kotak Mahindra Capital and Axis Capital, to helm its upcoming $1 Bn (₹9,634 Cr) public issue. However, this will not be InMobi’s first stab at an IPO. In 2021, it was reportedly planning for an IPO but shelved the plans due to adverse market conditions and funding winter. Leverage Edu Founded in 2017 by Akshay Chaturvedi, Leverage Edu is a study abroad platform that helps students apply to foreign universities. Its horizontal stack also spans offerings like fintech, accommodation, travel and career support. Besides its core app, it also offers test preparation courses for exams like IELTS and TOEFL. The startup claims to have so far catered to more than 1.75 Lakh customers. Leverage Edu has so far raised nearly $73 Mn from names such as Blume Ventures, DSG Consumer Partners, and Kaizenvest. In April 2026, Inc42 reported that Leverage Edu had begun discussions with both domestic and international investment bankers for an IPO. The startup is looking to raise ₹2,000 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr via its public issue, which will comprise both fresh issue of shares and an OFS component. The platform is eyeing a valuation of over $900 Mn. In September 2026, Inc42 reported that the startup was looking to raise a ₹500 Cr as part of a pre-IPO round . Sources further added that the company is in the process of finalising merchant bankers for its public issue and will file its DRHP with SEBI by 2027-end. On the financial front, Leverage Edu’s revenue from operations zoomed 91% to ₹173 Cr in FY25 from ₹90.6 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. In line with the top line, losses also rose nearly 56% to ₹106 Cr from ₹68 Cr in FY25. Mohalla Tech (ShareChat) Founded in 2015 by IIT Kanpur alumni Ankush Sachdeva, Bhanu Pratap Singh and Farid Ahsan, Mohalla Tech operates social media platform ShareChat, short video platform Moj and subscription-based microdrama app QuickTV. It has raised over $1.2 Bn in funding till date from names such as Lightspeed, Tiger Global, Temasek, Tencent, among others. Kicking off its IPO plans, Mohalla Tech cofounder and CFO, Manohar Charan, told a publication that the startup is targeting a public listing to raise over $400 Mn in the next four to five quarters (FY28). On the financial front, ShareChat managed to narrow its adjusted EBITDA loss by 72% to ₹219 Cr in FY25 from ₹793 Cr a year ago. However, its operating revenue remained nearly flat at ₹723 Cr as against ₹718 Cr in FY24. Navi Founded in 2018 by Flipkart cofounder Bansal and Ankit Agarwal, Navi is a fintech startup that offers a range of financial services such as loans, digital payments, insurance, and mutual fund investments. Reports in February 2025 first indicated that Navi was likely eyeing a public listing in the second half of FY26 . However, the startup later deferred its IPO plans. Subsequently in August 2026, reports once again surfaced that Navi was planning to file its DRHP with SEBI by December 2026 , eyeing a fresh issue-only IPO of about ₹3,000 Cr. The fintech unicorn is also said to have appointed JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as advisers for the proposed offering. Ahead of the IPO, Dutch VC giant Prosus in August 2026 also invested $100 Mn in the fintech startup , marking the latter’s first institutional capital raise. This isn’t Navi’s first attempt at going public. It first filed a DRHP with SEBI in 2022 for an ₹3,350 Cr offering but scrapped the plan amid market turbulence. On the financial front, Navi’s net loss widened 268.7% to ₹465.99 in FY26 from ₹126.4 Cr in the prior fiscal year. This came despite operating revenue increasing 16.8% to ₹2,981.7 Cr from ₹2,565 Cr in FY25. OfBusiness Founded in 2015 by Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra, Bhuvan Gupta, Chandranshu Sinha, Nitin Jain, Srinath Ramakkrushnan and Vasant Sridhar, OfBusiness runs a B2B ecommerce platform that sells construction materials and offers financing solutions to customers. In November 2024, the startup roped in five investment banks, namely Axis Capital, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Citigroup, and Bank of America, to helm its IPO. Right after, CFO Bhavesh Keswani revealed plans for a $750 Mn to $1 Bn public issue. However, the plan did not materialise. Reviving its IPO plans two years later, reports once again surfaced in August 2026 that the B2B ecommerce unicorn was looking to file its DRHP with SEBI by November 2026. This time, it is eyeing a $800 Mn IPO , which could comprise a fresh issue of up to $260 Mn and a $540 Mn OFS. OfBusiness is said to be targeting a valuation in the range of $5-6 Bn. On the financial front, the B2B ecommerce giant reported a 21% jump in its consolidated profit to ₹724 Cr in FY26 from ₹597 Cr in FY25. However, operating revenue remained largely flat YoY at ₹20,645 Cr. PayNearby Founded in 2016 by Anand Kumar Bajaj and Yashwant Lodha Subhash Kumar, PayNearby utilises its network of local retail shop owners to facilitate digital financial services for its customers. Its offerings include cash withdrawals, remittances, bill payments, deposits, and insurance. The fintech startup claims to have more than 12 Lakh retail partners under its belt and has raised nearly $4 Mn in funding to date. Kicking off its IPO preparations, cofounder and CEO Bajaj shared in August 2025 that PayNearby is eyeing a FY27 listing . The company is also finalising a merchant banker as it looks to file its DRHP with the SEBI soon. PayNearby’s standalone operating revenue slipped 4% to ₹355 Cr in FY24 from ₹368 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, profits fell 25% to ₹1.5 Cr from ₹2 Cr in FY23. PayU India Prosus-backed payments solutions provider PayU India’s IPO ambitions remain on hold. In June 2025, the Dutch giant announced it was deferring the listing to first strengthen its operations. This was the third time that the company delayed its IPO plans. Early 2025 reports had suggested that PayU was gearing up to file its DRHP for a post-Q1 FY26 markets debut, but the plans failed to materialise. Earlier in November 2023, Prosus’ then CIO Ervin Tu had projected readiness for a H2 2024 listing via a $500 Mn IPO. That plan also fizzled. The June 2025 postponement of the IPO followed a ₹1,013 Cr rights issue from parent Prosus in April 2025. Notably, a few months later in September, reports once again surfaced that the fintech major was looking to raise $250 Mn to $300 Mn in a pre-IPO round to broaden its investor base, test demand, and set a benchmark valuation for the listing. As per parent Prosus’ annual report, PayU India’s revenue climbed 21% to $669 Mn in FY25 from $551 Mn in the year ago fiscal. The investor also claimed that PayU’s India payment arm broke even in H2 FY25 while adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (aEBIT) margin improved by 1 percentage point to -2% in the financial year under review. Practo Founded in 2008 by Shashank ND and Abhinav Lal, Practo helps patients book appointments with doctors for online consultations, order medicines, and book diagnostic tests. It also offers software solutions for doctors, clinics, and hospitals. The startup also operates 40 co-branded dermatology clinics across the country. The health tech startup has raised nearly $230 Mn in funding to date from the likes of Tencent, Peak XV Partners (then Sequoia Capital), Z47 Partners (erstwhile Matrix Partners India), Sofina, among others. Practo was initially planning to list on the Indian bourses in 2026 but has now moved the IPO timeline to 2027. Ahead of the listing, in February 2026, reports surfaced that the startup was in advanced talks to raise up to $125 Mn in a pre-IPO round, in a mix of equity and debt, at a valuation of $700 Mn. The startup reported an operating EBITDA of ₹15 Cr on a revenue of ₹234 Cr in FY25. Rebel Foods Founded in 2011 by Kallol Banerjee and Jaydeep Barman, Rebel Foods is a cloud kitchen unicorn that operates multiple quick service restaurant (QSR) brands such as Behrouz Biryani, Ovenstory Pizza, The Good Bowl, SLAY Coffee, Wendy’s, among others. The startup has so far amassed over $563 Mn in funding from the likes of Coatue Management, Lightbox, Peak XV Partners, and Temasek. The startup was last pegged at $1.4 Bn during its last $25 Mn fundraise from Qatar Investment Authority in April 2025. The company’s IPO plans first came to light in October 2024 after reports surfaced that Rebel Foods was looking to list on the bourses in the next 18 months (April 2026). However, the company is yet to even file its DRHP. However, in a major top-level rejig in July 2025, the company’s cofounder and India CEO Ankush Grover was appointed as global CEO, while incumbent Jaydeep Barman was elevated to the role of chairman and group CEO. On the financial front, the unicorn’s net losses shrank 12% to ₹336.6 Cr in FY25 from ₹380.3 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, operating revenues grew 14% to ₹1,617.4 Cr from ₹1,420.2 Cr in FY24. Servify Founded in 2015 by Sreevathsa Prabhakar, Servify is a B2B device management platform that offers protection plans, buybacks, and exchanges. The startup earns a majority of its revenue from sale of services such as device protection plans and platform licences. Besides India, it also operates in the US, Canada, China and the Middle East. The startup has raised nearly $130 Mn in funding to date from BEENext, Blume Ventures, DMI Sparkle Fund, Iron Pillars, and others. Inc42 exclusively reported in January 2025 that the Mumbai-based startup had enlisted three investment bankers for a $400 Mn to $500 Mn IPO at a likely valuation of $1.5 Bn. The offering will likely lean heavily on OFS (55-60%), with the remaining 40-45% reserved for fresh issue of shares. Servify was previously looking to list on the exchanges by Q1 2026, but the plan looks far-fetched as the company is yet to even file its draft IPO papers with the markets regulator. Meanwhile, Servify saw hefty improvement on the financial front in FY24 as loss shrank 59% YoY to ₹93.81 Cr. This came largely on the back of operating revenue increasing 23% YoY to ₹754 Cr in the fiscal under review. Spinny Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh, Mohit Gupta, and Ganesh Pawar, Spinny operates a full-stack marketplace that enables users to buy and sell certified used cars. Unlike aggregators, the platform owns the inventory and refurbishes cars in-house. Backed by marquee names such as Fidelity, Accel, Tiger Global, General Catalyst and WestBridge Capital, the startup has raised more than $784 Mn in funding to date. It was last valued at around $1.5 Bn during its $170 Mn fundraise, which was a mix of primary and secondary deals, in early-2026. It competes with the likes of CARS24, CarDekho, and Droom in India’s growing used car market. Kicking off its IPO proceedings, Spinny, in April 2026, roped in Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup as bankers for its potential IPO. In September 2026, the startup pre-filed its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential route. The Gurugram-based startup is looking to raise ₹2,500 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr through a combination of fresh issue and an OFS component. It is targeting a potential listing in 2027. On the financial front, Spinny’s net loss declined 28% to ₹423.8 Cr in FY25 from ₹590.3 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Operating revenue rose 25% to ₹4,656.1 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹3,730 Cr in FY24. Square Yards Founded in 2014 by husband-wife duo Tanuj Shori and Kanika Gupta Shori, Square Yards runs a full-stack proptech platform for property search, property management tools, and home interior financing. The startup has raised more than $200 Mn in funding from Reliance Group, ADM Capital, Bennett Coleman & Co Ltd (BCCL), Genkai Capital, and others. In May 2026, Square Yards’ CFO Piyush Bothra told Inc42 that the company was looking to rope in bankers to explore a $250-300 Mn IPO in the next 12 months. If the IPO materialises, Square Yards will be among a handful of Indian startups where founders will continue to hold more than 50% stake. On the financial front, the proptech startup clocked an operating revenue of ₹2,086 Cr in FY26 on a gross profit of ₹476 Cr. Udaan Founded in 2016 by Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan operates a B2B-focused ecommerce platform. Operating across categories like FMCG, staples and fruits & vegetables, the platform also facilitates supply chain and logistics solutions for retailers. It also has a fintech platform called udaanCapital, which offers financial services to small businesses and helps them with their working capital requirements. Backed by marquee names such as Lightspeed, DST Global, Altimeter Capital and Tencent, Udaan has raised more than $2.17 Bn in funding to date. In March 2026, Udaan’s cofounder and CEO Vaibhav Gupta told a publication that the company was eyeing a listing on the Indian bourses in the next nine to 18 months. Gupta added that the B2B ecommerce major plans to commence the process of redomiciling back to India from Singapore “soon”. On the financial front, Udaan reported a 37% YoY decline in net loss to ₹1,055 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue also declined 20% YoY to ₹4,561 Cr during the fiscal under review. Wonderchef Founded in 2009 by celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor and Ravi Saxena, Wonderchef sells a range of kitchenware and home appliances such as coffee machine, mixer grinders, cast iron pans, among others. The startup sells its offerings via its own website, ecommerce platforms as well as its own exclusive business outlets (EBOs). Backed by the likes of Sixth Sense Ventures, Amicus Capital, Godrej Family Office, Malpani Group, among others, the brand has raised more than $30 Mn in funding to date. The D2C brand was mulling filing its DRHP with SEBI for an OFS-heavy IPO at a likely valuation of ₹1,800 Cr. This is double compared to Wonderchef’s last-known valuation of ₹900 Cr. The D2C brand’s net profit soared 300% to ₹6 Cr in FY25 as against a profit of ₹1.6 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Revenue from operations jumped 13.9% to ₹430 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹377.7 Cr in FY24. Zypp Electric Founded in 2017 by Akash Gupta and Tushar Mehta, Zypp offers EV-based mobility solutions for delivery workers. Besides the core EV leasing business, it also operates EV battery swapping, maintenance and servicing infrastructure. It also runs an advertising business and has developed a fleet management software platform, called Fleekies.ai. Backed by the likes of Japan’s ENEOS Group, 100Unicorns, Anthill Ventures and Venture Catalysts, the EV logistics startup has raised more than $75 Mn in funding to date. In June 2026, cofounder and CEO Gupta told Inc42 that Zypp Electric has roped in Axis Capital, SBI Capital Markets and DAM Capital to manage its upcoming public offering. He said the startup is looking to raise up to $200 Mn (about ₹1,890 Cr) via its IPO within the next 18 to 24 months. Ahead of the listing, Zypp Electric is looking to raise a pre-IPO round in the range of $40-50 Mn from private equity firms and impact-focused funds. On the financial front, Zypp Electric’s revenue from operations zoomed 49% to ₹438 Cr in FY25 from ₹293 Cr in the previous year. Meanwhile, net loss widened 20.1% to ₹107.5 Cr from ₹89.5 Cr in FY24. title: Starlink, Jio & OneWeb: Untangling The Satcom Queue
content: The irony was not lost on many. Around the same time as the internet in India’s national capital Delhi was shut down for several hours amid massive security and incessant protests, SpaceXAI chairman and founder Elon Musk waded into one of his quintessential Twitter feuds with the Indian government over Starlink and its satellite internet services. This time, his target was not just the Indian government. Musk took on Reliance Jio — and then Mukesh Ambani too — accusing the conglomerate of strong-arming the government into creating a monopoly when it comes to satellite internet or satcom services. He even called Ambani the Prime Minister of India. “Starlink is licensed in over 165 countries and has spent five years complying with every single law and requirement of the government of India, so why still no license?” Musk posted , asking whether Ambani is the “real boss of India”. Out came the responses from all quarters of India. Reliance Industries rejected suggestions that it fears competition, saying it welcomes satellite broadband players, including Starlink, provided they follow Indian laws and policies. Reliance also pointed out that Jio’s satellite services are awaiting clearances. The Ministry of Communications, meanwhile, has denied allegations of unequal treatment. It said the authorisation framework is fair and non-discriminatory, and that Starlink, Reliance Jio and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb are at “broadly the same regulatory stage.” And then, Starlink responded to Reliance saying, “We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely – and all with the requisite government approvals.” Everyone’s Waiting In The Queue The immediate question is what Starlink means by having the “requisite government approvals”. Its statement does not explicitly say that its security assessment is complete or that spectrum has been assigned. Those are separate steps from obtaining a satellite communications licence and an IN-SPACe authorisation, and they stand between the operators and commercial launch. The DoT has taken a similar line on the approval process. It said all three operators have received GMPCS licences and that security assessments remain underway. Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite (GMPCS) is a satellite-based communication system that provides voice, data, fax, and messaging services directly to portable terminals anywhere on ground. The DoT added that spectrum assignment will follow once the relevant assessments are complete. So a licence does not, by itself, authorise a company to start commercial services. Operators must meet the conditions attached to their services, clear the security process and complete spectrum-related requirements. The dates of approvals have become part of the debate. Eutelsat OneWeb received its GMPCS licence in August 2021 and IN-SPACe authorisation in November 2023. Jio’s satellite communications arm received its GMPCS licence in March 2022. Starlink received its GMPCS licence in June 2025 and IN-SPACe authorisation in July 2025. However, this timeline does not tell the full story. According to a Financial Express report citing DoT records, Jio Satellite Communications Limited (JSCL) completed its security and technical compliance demonstration on March 20, 2025, while Eutelsat OneWeb conducted its demonstration in January 2025. Starlink’s demonstration took place only in early 2026. So if anything, OneWeb should be ahead of Starlink and Jio in the queue after the final assessments. Bharti Enterprises chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said OneWeb had applied for approval five years ago, its ground network had been ready for three years, and its satellites had been positioned over India for around five years. Mittal added OneWeb would be happy to receive approval “at least a few days before him [Musk].” The different timelines do not, on their own, establish that one company has been favoured or that others are being held back. They also do not explain what conditions remain outstanding or unfulfilled in each case. Therefore, the relevant questions are which requirements each operator has met, what is still pending and whether the same standard and timelines apply to all three players. This will help us get to the bottom of the questions that Musk has raised. The Regulator Takes Its Time Sohom Banerjee, a public policy and technology strategist and founder of Quantive Advisory LLP, said the delay raises questions about regulator predictability, but is not in itself proof of unequal treatment. A fair process, he argued, requires equivalent security standards, documented criteria, clarity on outstanding requirements and a defined next step for each applicant. Banerjee also cautioned against treating proposed timelines for one regulatory stage as deadlines for the entire process. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India’s suggested 30-day window for spectrum assignment and objections relates to a stage after prior in-principle network clearance. It should not be interpreted as a deadline for completing security assessments. The criteria for security assessment are not open for public discussion or consultation, but given that internet services are critical not just for civilian use but also defence infrastructure, experts presume that such assessments may not necessarily take the same time for each applicant. The approval process involves four distinct steps: a GMPCS licence, IN-SPACe authorisation, security assessment and spectrum assignment. Conflating them and calling this a single approval is what complicates the narrative. Starlink May Be Ready, But Is That All It Takes? Starlink’s latest statement is a claim about its preparation and infrastructure, but this does not indicate anything about whether the Indian government has completed its diligence when it comes to the security assessment. While Starlink says it has built dedicated systems and gateways in India to serve Indian traffic, and that these have the requisite government approvals, this is not a guarantee of spectrum allocation. The distinction is also relevant to Reliance Jio. In its IPO papers, Jio Platforms identified satellite broadband as a potential competitor to JioFiber and JioAirfiber, particularly in areas where terrestrial networks are expensive or difficult to deploy. It also flagged that administrative allocation of satellite spectrum could give satellite operators a different cost structure from terrestrial telecom players that acquire spectrum through auctions. It’s imperative to understand the structure. Jio Satellite Communications Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Jio Platforms, was incorporated in October 2021 to provide communications services, including satellite-based connectivity. It reported revenue from operations of ₹34.3 Cr in FY26 up from ₹10.7 Cr in FY25, against no revenue in FY24. The company reported ₹10.5 Cr for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. These figures relate to the subsidiary and should not be read as revenue from a launched retail satellite broadband service. The filings also identify uncertainties around the timing, approvals and competitiveness of Jio’s own satellite plans. The company therefore has a commercial stake in the rules governing satellite broadband, even as its services await clearance. And indeed, that has to be made amply clear: no company has launched satellite internet services in India yet. Banerjee said predictable regulation does not mean relaxing security checks. It means setting out the criteria, identifying the authority responsible for each decision and communicating what remains to be done. Security checks are central to satellite broadband because the operator controls parts of a communications network that may be used in strategically sensitive areas. The assessment needs to establish how India can retain oversight of network operations, access to sensitive information and service continuity. One could also argue that this is a cultural difference, that Musk is used to a different governance approach when it comes to such matters. A security clearance is part of the overall approvals in the US, for example, and not a separate process. Tarun Wig, cofounder and CEO of Innefu Labs, said foreign-controlled satellite networks can create risks around data sovereignty, service continuity and external control over critical communications infrastructure, particularly during conflicts. Starlink’s role in Ukraine has brought those concerns into focus, he said, though the circumstances there do not automatically mean India would face the same risks. Wig said India should have a security framework in place before these services launch. He pointed to data protection and localisation requirements where necessary, network security audits, encryption, lawful interception under Indian law, incident reporting and safeguards against unauthorised access and cyberattacks. Banerjee spoke on the operational control aspects of the security assessment. He believes that relevant checks could examine who can activate terminals, change routing or coverage, access sensitive network information and suspend services. Domestic control over key network functions, auditable access, terminal identification, restrictions in sensitive areas and clear incident-reporting processes likely also form part of the assessment. The commercial case for satellite broadband is clear in places where fibre and mobile networks are difficult or costly to extend. TRAI data for August 2026 recorded 48.63 Mn wired broadband connections and 19.34 Mn fixed wireless connections. Satellite services could help connect remote communities and businesses including mines, energy sites, schools and health centres. Their reach will depend on pricing, network capacity and the conditions attached to spectrum. The government’s position is that all three operators remain subject to the same security process. But to settle questions about delay and unequal treatment, it will need to make the next steps clearer: which requirements remain pending for each operator, who must sign off and what needs to happen before spectrum is assigned. Starlink says it’s ready to launch but is not being allowed to. Reliance says it doesn’t fear competition. OneWeb says it’s also waiting in the queue. Ultimately, no one has launched anything yet, so all of this seems more like a case of Musk’s impatience. Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam Creatives: Abhyam Gusai The post Starlink, Jio & OneWeb: Untangling The Satcom Queue appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: Indian Listed New-Age Tech Company Tracker: Market Cap, Revenue & More
content: For years, we at Inc42 have tracked the Indian tech startup ecosystem and seen it grow from a kid to an adult. Among the clearest signs of evolution and maturity of this ecosystem is the growing number of startups eyeing a public listing now. For Indian companies, achieving a public listing has for long symbolised operational progression, transparency, and long-term viability. For startups, it’s a relatively new but increasingly critical rite of passage, one that not only signals coming of age but also creates pathways for investor exits and wealth creation. Currently, a handful of startups, including the likes of Razorpay, PRISM, PhonePe, among others, are in various stages of their IPO journey . Meanwhile, over 70 Indian new-age tech companies have already crossed the milestone and are now listed on the bourses. The list also includes Indian companies like MakeMyTrip and Freshworks, which are listed on Nasdaq in the US. India’s startup IPO wave reached its peak in 2025, surpassing the previous year’s momentum. While 18 startups listed in 2025, 13 startups have already reached that milestone in 2026. With companies like Cult.fit, Moneyview, others, eyeing to tap the public markets this year, the list is only expected to grow further this year. 15 new-age companies — AceVector, Moneyview, Rentomojo, ESDS, Purple Style Labs, Turtlemint, Klassroom, Shiprocket, LEAP India, Kissht, Aye Finance, Fractal Analytics, Amagi, Shadowfax and SEDEMAC — have made their public market debut in 2026. Defence tech company Tonbo Imaging and manufacturing startup Zetwerk are set to make their public markets debut next week. Inside The Dalal Street Startup Ride Indian startups had gained a reputation for being “loss making” by prioritising growth at all costs and market share over immediate profitability. The trend of putting scale ahead of the bottom line was at its peak amid the funding boom of 2020-22. While prioritising growth is not wrong for startups, especially at early stages, the start of funding winter in 2022 gave a reality check to the Indian startup ecosystem. Subsequently, startups started pushing for profitability. Giving further wings to the aggressive profitability push was the ambition to list on the exchanges. While new-age tech companies look to turn profitable before filing their draft IPO papers, those that cross the line manage to stay in the green, data shows. Over 60 of the new-age tech companies are currently profitable. In terms of profits, Groww now leads the pack of new-age tech companies, posting a net profit of ₹2,083 Cr in FY26. Prominent internet companies Paytm and Eternal trail Groww in terms of profitability, raking in profits of ₹ 553 Cr and ₹ 366 Cr in FY26, respectively. It is pertinent to mention that these companies have been listed on the bourses for years now, with Info Edge making its public market debut in 2006. While these companies trace their origin back to the 90s, a large majority of the new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s purview are about a decade old. From a broad perspective, Inc42 data reflects that the median time taken for a startup to get listed on the bourses is 11 years. While listing for 18-year-old ixigo and 19-year-old Fino Payments Bank came relatively much later, ArisInfra’s IPO materialised within four years of its operations. Meanwhile, the new-age tech companies that have made their public market debuts this year generally turned profitable right before their public market debuts. For instance, eyewear major Lenskart reported a net profit of around ₹297 Cr , a significant turnaround from a ₹10 Cr loss in FY24. The company maintained profitability in FY26, raking in a PAT of ₹494 Cr in the fiscal. Urban Company also reported its first consolidated net profit of approximately ₹ 240 Cr for FY25, it returned to the red in FY26. For the full year FY26, the company reported a net loss of ₹234.8 Cr against a net profit of ₹239.8 Cr in previous year despite seeing a revenue growth of 36% YoY to ₹1,555.5 Cr Sectors Driving India’s Startup IPO Boom The startup sectors producing the most number of listed companies is proportional to the private funding trends witnessed in the Indian startup ecosystem. The three most funded sectors, fintech, ecommerce and enterprise tech, also house the highest number listed startups. While fintech and ecommerce house 14 names each, 13 enterprise tech startups have listed on the bourses so far. The dominance of the fintech and ecommerce sectors on the bourses is expected to continue as the likes of Tonbo Imaging, Zepto and OYO would soon be making their public market debuts. Delhi NCR Home To Highest Number Of Listed Startups While Bengaluru continues to be the startup capital of India, Delhi and its neighbouring cities Gurugram and Noida account for the most number of listed new-age tech companies . Overall, the Delhi NCR region is home to 25 listed new-age tech companies, ahead of Bengaluru’s sixteen and Mumbai’s thirteen. While fifteen companies, including Eternal, Delhivery, and Lenskart, call Gurugram their home, Awfis, EaseMyTrip, MapmyIndia and E2E Networks are from Delhi. Noida on the other hand is home to six listed new-age tech companies, including Paytm and IndiQube. Delhi NCR contributes $93.4 Bn in the cumulative $173 Bn market cap of new-age tech companies. title: Burma Burma Parent’s FY26 Loss Surges 31X YoY To ₹15 Cr
content: Restaurant chain Burma Burma’s parent entity, Hunger Pangs Limited, saw its net loss skyrocket nearly 31X to ₹15.4 Cr in the fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26) compared to ₹50 Lakh in the previous fiscal year. According to its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), the restaurant chain’s revenue from operations also zoomed 46.6% to ₹155.5 Cr in the fiscal under review from ₹106.1 Cr in FY25. Including other income of ₹1.5 Cr, Burma Burma’s total income stood at ₹157 Cr in FY26. On the operational front, the restaurant chain’s EBITDA also climbed 20.2% to ₹25.7 Cr in FY26 from ₹21.4 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Besides its FY26 financials, the DRHP also shed light on the company’s Q1 FY27 numbers. Burma Burma’s parent reported a net profit of ₹1.1 Cr in the quarter under review against an operating revenue of ₹53.7 Cr. Given total expenses of ₹55.2 Cr during the quarter, what helped the company mint a profit in Q1 FY27 was ₹1.98 Cr in deferred tax credits. Burma Burma also reported an EBITDA profit of ₹11.4 Cr in the quarter ended June 2026, while the EBITDA margin stood at 21.3%. Founded in 2013 by Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer, Hunger Pangs operates premium casual restaurant chain Burma Burma, which serves vegetarian Burmese cuisine. It competes with the likes of brands such as Mainland China, Mamagoto, Yum Yum Cha, and Berco’s. At the end of July 2026, it operated 22 restaurants across nine cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Delhi NCR. After raising $4 Mn at a valuation of over $50 Mn earlier this year, the hospitality chain has now filed its DRHP with markets regulator SEBI. Its proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.8 Cr shares. Of the fresh IPO proceeds, Burma Burma plans to use ₹117.3 Cr to open 27 new company-owned outlets by FY29. The remaining capital will be used for general corporate purposes. Notably, Hunger Pangs disclosed in its DRHP that it plans to launch a new brand. “We have conceptualised a premium casual dining chain of Japanese restaurants and noodle shops, with influences of Buddhist traditions,” read the document. Where Did Burma Burma Spend In FY26? In line with its revenue growth, Burma Burma’s spending also saw a major uptick. The company’s total expenses zoomed 61.8% YoY to ₹175.8 Cr in FY26. Let’s dive deeper into the company’s expenditure. Employee Benefits Expenses: Representing the company’s largest cost head, Burma Burma’s personnel costs surged 53.3% YoY to ₹50.7 Cr in FY26 from ₹33.1 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Cost Of Materials Consumed: Burma Burma spent ₹30.4 Cr on raw materials and kitchen supplies in the fiscal under review, 51% higher than ₹20.1 Cr in FY25. Finance Cost: The restaurant chain’s interest and borrowing-related expenses grew 70% YoY to ₹6.6 Cr in the year under review. Other Expenses: Spending under this line item also grew 54.6% YoY to ₹48.8 Cr in the fiscal year ended March 2026. title: Decoding Urban Company’s ₹2,500 Cr Fundraise Proposal
content: Listed home services major Urban Company’s board approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr yesterday, seeking to shore up its war chest at a critical juncture. On one hand, Urban Company’s instant home services business, InstaHelp, is facing stiff competition. Fighting rivals Snabbit and Pronto for a slice of the market has turned out to be an expensive affair , with spending on InstaHelp contributing to Urban Company’s widening losses. At the same time, the company is looking to expand its product lineup under the Native brand by entering the residential air conditioner market. Meanwhile, its bread and butter consumer services continue to generate stable results. Urban Company’s financials reflect these pressures. The company reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹144 Cr in Q2 FY27, driven by a ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. Excluding InstaHelp, it reported an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹30 Cr. During the quarter, consolidated revenue from operations grew 41.4% YoY to ₹537.3 Cr , while total expenses increased 61.5% to ₹745.7 Cr. Consequently, the company’s consolidated net loss more than tripled to ₹182.5 Cr from ₹59.3 Cr in the year-ago period. However, the management maintains that Urban Company can meet its profitability targets without the proposed fundraise Yet, the management has rejected the suggestion that the fundraise is necessary to offset InstaHelp’s impact on its financials. How Badly Does Urban Company Need The Cash? Urban Company has positioned the proposed ₹2,500 Cr fundraise as a means to bolster its balance sheet and provide greater flexibility to invest across its businesses. “Our ambition is to go beyond being just a home services company and eventually become the trusted home platform for Indian consumers – almost the operating system for the Indian home. So given that ambition, we want the strategic flexibility over the next few years to invest in all our areas of business,” CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal told analysts during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call. The company also plans to deploy the capital towards growth opportunities, including acquisitions. While no acquisition deals have been finalised till now, the management is evaluating opportunities that could help Urban Company consolidate its position in an existing market or enter a new category. Bhal added that the company would take an opportunistic approach to international markets and Native. However, an acquisition in InstaHelp would be “highly unlikely”. “If at all we do an M&A, it would be to add on categories that we don’t operate in today where we feel that the decision of build versus buy may be tilting in favour of buy,” he noted. Urban Company has guided for adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 Cr in adjusted EBITDA profit by FY31. The management maintained that its current financial position, even without raising additional capital, is sufficient to meet these targets. However, Bhal acknowledged that the company’s existing balance sheet limits its financial flexibility, given InstaHelp’s losses. While the management maintains that the company can meet its profitability targets without additional capital, the proposed fundraise would provide it with greater room to invest in growth and respond to changing market conditions. In particular, Urban Company is facing intense competition in the emerging quick home services segment. For instance, after Urban Company disclosed that InstaHelp completed 6.2 Mn orders in Q2, Snabbit’s founder Aayush Agarwal claimed that the startup had served 6.45 Mn orders during the period. Diving Into A New Market While it faces intense competition in the quick home services market, Urban Company is simultaneously looking to expand into a new category. Alongside approving the fundraise proposal, its board proposed exploring residential air conditioners as a new business under its consumer appliances brand Native, whose portfolio currently comprises water purifiers and smart locks. “We’ve now operated in the segment of air conditioning servicing and repair for close to 11-12 years, ever since the inception of the company. And there’s a lot of data and knowledge that we have gathered on what are the consumer pain points and what are some of the unmet needs of the consumers. Based on those data points and our own understanding of the market and the unmet needs, we have been quietly working on creating an innovative cutting-edge product,” Bhal told analysts on the call. The company is yet to disclose further details, including a commercial launch timeline. Notably, Inc42 reported last year about Urban Company’s potential foray into AC business . Bhal said the first one to two years in the new market would focus on learning and gathering customer feedback. He also noted that Urban Company’s app would be the sole distribution channel for its ACs. The CEO emphasised a “calibrated and measured” approach to capital allocation, adding that Native has a clear path to profitability that should not be affected by the new venture. For context, Native’s net transaction value (NTV) grew 35.4% YoY in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue rose 40% to ₹105 Cr. The segment remained loss-making on an adjusted EBITDA basis, reporting a loss of ₹9 Cr. However, loss as a percentage of NTV declined to 6.8% from 9% a year ago. Urban Company’s platform sees 10X as many AC servicing, repair, and installation orders as water purifier orders, giving it a larger existing customer base for AC-related services. This provides a potential channel to market Native’s ACs, although service demand does not necessarily translate into appliance sales. With InstaHelp facing stiff competition and Native preparing to enter a new product category, Urban Company is pursuing multiple growth opportunities even as its losses widen. The proposed fundraise would provide additional capital to support these plans, although the management maintains that the company can achieve its stated profitability targets without it. title: Nazara, Groww Gain Among New-Age Tech Stocks This Week, AceVector Falls 18%
content: Fewer than half of the 67 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage advanced this week despite a broader market recovery. While 31 stocks gained between 0.03% and 17.63%, 36 declined, with losses reaching 18.43%. Snapdeal parent AceVector was the biggest loser, falling 18.43% to ₹24.97, about 12% below its listing price. Market intelligence platform Tracxn followed, declining 8.26% to ₹31.78. IndiQube and Veefin lost more than 7% each. ixigo, EaseMyTrip, Swiggy, and Fractal touched fresh 52-week lows, while Nazara, Zelio, and E2E Networks hit fresh 52-week highs this week. NSE SME-listed Yudiz led gains, surging 17.63% to ₹24.35, although it remained over 85% below its listing price. Nazara, ideaForge, DevX, and FirstCry were among the other gainers. The combined market capitalisation of the 67 companies increased by $5.84 Bn to $160.55 Bn from $154.71 Bn at the end of the previous week. Now, let’s take a look at the key developments at the new-age tech companies this week. E2E Networks Swings To Profit E2E Networks posted a consolidated net profit of ₹72.7 Cr in Q2 FY27 against a ₹13.5 Cr loss a year earlier. Operating revenue jumped 411% to ₹223.8 Cr from ₹43.8 Cr. Separately, it paid fines of ₹10,000 each, plus GST, to NSE and BSE for failing to provide prior intimation of its August 31 board meeting. The cloud infrastructure company said it would strengthen compliance monitoring to prevent recurrence. NCLT Dismisses Globalbees Insolvency Plea The NCLT dismissed an insolvency application against FirstCry subsidiary Globalbees filed by Ashutosh Garg, Paritosh Garg, and Manju Agarwal over an alleged ₹64.92 Cr claim, plus 18% annual interest. Separately, Globalbees extended the deadline for its ₹5.69 Cr sale of its entire 51.54% stake in textile brand Mush to November 30. The buyers are existing shareholder Nihar Gosalia and Vaishvik Brahmbhatt. Fairfax Proposes Go Digit Stake Transfer Fairfax proposed transferring its interests in Go Digit General Insurance and Go Digit Life Insurance to IDBI Bank. Separately, Fairfax India Holdings also proposed transferring its entire IIFL Capital Services stake to the lender. The proposals follow the selection of a wholly owned Fairfax Financial subsidiary to acquire a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank for approximately ₹52,878 Cr. The transfers would expand IDBI’s insurance and investment services presence, subject to requisite approvals. Lenskart Faces Customs Demand Lenskart received an order during the week demanding ₹6.59 Cr in differential customs duty and ₹6.58 Cr in penalty, totalling ₹13.17 Cr, plus unquantified interest. The authority reclassified certain imported optical eyeframes with clip-ons. The company said it considers the order contestable and plans to appeal. First Games’ GST Demand Reduced Paytm joint venture First Games Technology received a ₹703.66 Cr GST demand for April 2018 to March 2023, down from ₹5,712 Cr proposed in an April 2025 show-cause notice. An equivalent penalty and applicable interest are additional. First Games is evaluating its statutory options. BlackBuck Restructures Loads Business BlackBuck approved transferring its loads business to wholly owned subsidiary BlackBuck Transport Services through a slump sale to improve operational efficiency. The business generated ₹88.74 Cr in FY26 revenue, equivalent to 12.6% of BlackBuck’s standalone total income, and had net worth of ₹98.8 Lakh. Aequs’ Amalgamation Proposal Rejected The Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ regional director of South Western Region rejected Aequs’ amalgamation with wholly owned subsidiaries AeroStructures Manufacturing India, Aequs Engineered Plastics, and Aequs Force Consumer Products. The order cited non-compliance with Section 233 of the Companies Act: shareholder approval representing 88.9% of total share value against the required 90%, uncertain delivery of postal ballot notices, pending labour cases, and missing BSE and NSE no-objection certificates. Aequs is considering refiling or seeking approval under Section 232. With that, here’s a look at the performance of the broader market this week. IT Leads Market Recovery The Sensex gained 3.11% to 74,729.27 this week, while the Nifty 50 rose 2.78% to 23,146.15. IT led sectoral gains at 11.72%, although participation beyond large-cap stocks remained muted. Geojit Investments’ research head Vinod Nair attributed the recovery to improving rupee sentiment, softer crude prices, easing bond yields, and strong quarterly business updates. The IMF’s higher growth forecasts for India for FY27 and FY28 also supported sentiment. Investors tracked RBI’s measures to manage public-sector oil marketing companies’ dollar demand and tighten rupee-linked forex derivatives rules. Effective October 16, banks’ minimum daily CRR maintenance rose to 99% of the prescribed requirement from 90%. Inflationary pressures, elevated crude oil prices, and continued foreign investor outflows remained concerns for the market. FIIs remained net sellers for the ninth consecutive week, although their net selling moderated to ₹8,991 Cr from ₹30,294 Cr in the previous week. However, they turned net buyers yesterday, with net purchases of ₹1,166 Cr. DIIs remained net buyers for the ninth straight week, investing ₹7,813 Cr. Month-to-date purchases of ₹48,168 Cr nearly offset FII selling of ₹48,769 Cr, according to Bajaj Broking. Investors will track September infrastructure output, October flash PMI readings, and the minutes of RBI’s monetary policy committee meeting. Earnings of major lenders will also be in focus, alongside results from Infosys, Swiggy, Eternal, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, and Tata Motors. Nair said sustaining the recovery would require earnings growth beyond IT, with financials, consumption, and industrials’ revenue and margins under scrutiny. Now, let’s take a deeper look at the performance of Nazara Technologies and Groww this week: Nazara Gains Amid Leadership Changes Nazara gained 10.02% to ₹416.80 amid a reshuffle that saw founder Nitish Mittersain move from MD to a non-executive role . The company’s board approved CaratLane founder Mithun Sacheti’s five-year appointment as whole-time director, designated executive director, subject to shareholder approval. Arun Agrawal, former global CFO of Ness Digital Engineering, will succeed outgoing CFO Rakesh Shah. Whole-time director Rohit Sharma will step down from January 1, 2027. The changes follow the $303 Mn acquisition of Spanish gaming companies Bluetile Games and BestPlay Systems and a ₹733.5 Cr preferential fundraise to finance it. On the financial front, Nazara posted a ₹82.5 Cr loss in Q1 FY27, with operating revenue falling 14% YoY to ₹428.8 Cr. Bluetile’s EBITDA remained flat despite 54% revenue growth amid higher user acquisition costs. Groww Gains Despite Flat Sequential Revenue Groww gained 4.34% to close the week ₹200.70 after its Q2 FY27 net profit rose 54% YoY to ₹724.7 Cr and operating revenue increased 47.4% YoY to ₹1,501.5 Cr. Sequentially, revenue was almost unchanged and profit fell 1.4% from ₹735 Cr. EBITDA slipped to ₹969 Cr from ₹971 Cr in the preceding June quarter. Growth in margin trading and commodity derivatives offset a 14.3% QoQ decline in equity derivatives revenue. The company attributed the decline in equity derivatives revenue to adjustments following the closing auction system’s (CAS) introduction. Expenses rose 28.5% YoY to ₹555.9 Cr, reflecting higher technology costs, AI-linked and other compute cost inflation, and ₹13 Cr in client reimbursements following a third-party market infrastructure institution’s operational issue. Groww AMC’s assets under management rose 145% YoY to ₹7,179 Cr, although it posted a ₹8.3 Cr quarterly loss. Separately, brokerage Jefferies reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on Groww following SEBI’s changes to the CAS framework. The revised rules include a shorter cash-market auction window and changes to the settlement-price calculation for index derivatives on expiry days. The updated framework is scheduled to be effective December 7, 2026. Jefferies expects lower expiry-day volatility and regulatory uncertainty to benefit brokers more than exchanges, whose premium turnover has already recovered to pre-CAS levels. title: FY26 Financial Tracker: Tracking The Financial Performance Of Indian Startups
content: The Indian startup ecosystem continued to mature in FY26, with 22 new-age tech companies making their public market debut as against 13 in FY25. At the same time, a growing number of startups turned profitable or moved closer to profitability after years of cost rationalisation to adjust to the new funding realities. Despite a tough Q4 for many startups due to geopolitical uncertainties, Indian startups are expected to improve their top and bottom line numbers in FY26. Of the 102 startups in the tracker, 65, or about 63.7%, reported profits in FY26. However, the profitability picture remained uneven. Together, these 65 startups generated a net profit of ₹14,511.8 Cr, while the remaining 37 posted a cumulative loss of ₹30,950.8 Cr, underscoring that sustainable profitability remains a work in progress for a section of the ecosystem. Even so, the scale of India’s startup ecosystem continued to expand. The 102 companies generated ₹4.75 Lakh Cr in operating revenue in FY26, a sharp 34.62% increase from ₹3.53 Lakh Cr in FY25. To help you track the financial health of new-age tech companies, Inc42 has launched the FY26 Financial Tracker , bringing together key financial metrics in one place. The tracker will be updated periodically with the latest financial disclosures and deeper insights into the performance of India’s startup ecosystem. So, without further ado, here’s a look at how Indian startups fared financially in FY26. Editor’s Note: This list is not a ranking of any kind, the companies have been placed alphabetically. This is a running list and will be updated periodically. title: Cleartrip’s FY26 Loss Widens 28% YoY To ₹805 Cr, Revenue Up 21%
content: Flipkart-owned travel platform Cleartrip’s net loss widened 28.1% YoY to ₹805 Cr in FY26 from ₹628.4 Cr in FY25, as its expenses continued to outpace revenue growth. The online travel aggregator’s operating revenue grew 20.8% to ₹198.3 Cr during the year from ₹164.1 Cr in the previous fiscal. Including other income, Cleartrip reported total income of around ₹241.3 Cr, compared with ₹366.7 Cr in FY25. Other income declined 34.2% YoY to ₹43 Cr. Meanwhile, spending on cashbacks and discounts rose 47.5% to ₹897.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹608.2 Cr a year earlier, outpacing top line growth. Cleartrip generated ₹702.2 Cr from service charges and ₹378.4 Cr from commissions and incentives before accounting for cashbacks and discounts, taking the combined figure to around ₹1,095.7 Cr. These figures should be distinguished from the operating revenue reported in its financial statements. Founded in 2006 by Hrush Bhatt, Matthew Spacie and Stuart Crighton, Cleartrip enables users to book flights, hotels, trains, buses and local activities through its website and app. Ecommerce major Flipkart acquired the company in 2021. Cleartrip’s accumulated losses rose to ₹3,828 Cr as of March 31, 2026, from ₹3,023 Cr a year earlier. Its negative net worth also widened to ₹3,066 Cr from ₹2,262 Cr in FY25. In its financial statements, the company said its ability to continue as a going concern depended on the success of its operations and its ability to secure funding. However, it added that its holding company, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, had provided a commitment and letter of financial support. During FY26, Cleartrip borrowed ₹3,964 Cr from Flipkart Internet and repaid ₹3,653 Cr. Interest on these loans stood at ₹130.4 Cr for the year. The widening loss comes as Cleartrip seeks to reduce its reliance on discounts and diversify beyond flight bookings. In July 2026, the company said it was targeting operational break-even by the end of FY27. Its plans include growing its hotels, trains and buses businesses and increasing revenue from ancillary services. The company has also seen leadership changes in recent years. Anuj Rathi, who joined as CBO, stepped down in June 2025, less than a year after his appointment, to launch his venture, profound.me. He was succeeded by former Flipkart executive Manjari Singhal, who previously led the ecommerce company’s beauty, FMCG and general merchandise businesses as vice-president and business head. Before Rathi’s departure, long-standing CEO Ayyappan Rajagopal resigned from Cleartrip in August 2024 to launch quick-commerce startup FirstClub . Where Did Cleartrip Spend? Cleartrip’s total expenses increased 21.9% YoY to ₹1,045.9 Cr in FY26 from ₹858.2 Cr in FY25 . Against operating revenue of ₹198.3 Cr, this translated into expenditure of ₹5.27 for every rupee earned from operations. Advertisement & Sales Promotion: Cleartrip’s spending on advertising and sales promotion rose 30.9% YoY to ₹133.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹102.2 Cr a year earlier. Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs increased 7.8% to ₹258.1 Cr from ₹239.4 Cr in FY25. Payment Gateway Charges: Payment processing expenses rose 40% YoY to ₹110.1 Cr from ₹78.7 Cr. Commission & Brokerage: Expenses under this head increased 33.2% YoY to ₹171.5 Cr from ₹128.8 Cr in FY25. title: Flipkart’s Logistics Arm Ekart Cuts FY26 Loss By 98% To ₹26 Cr
content: Instakart Services, the Flipkart-owned logistics company behind Ekart, nearly broke even in the fiscal year ending March 2026 (FY26). Its loss narrowed 98.3% to ₹26 Cr in the fiscal under review, compared to ₹1,508 Cr in FY25. The brand’s revenue from contracts with customers fell 4.2% to ₹13,194 Cr in FY26, from ₹13,779 Cr in the previous fiscal year. In this, Flipkart itself contributed ₹9,112 Cr, or about 69% of the total operating revenue. Operationally, logistics, transportation and shipping contributed the most share, approximately 50% to ₹6,419 Cr in the reported year. Revenue from this vertical plunged 39.5% YoY. Ekart also generates revenue from collection services and warehousing services. Collection services income fell 68% to ₹510 Cr, while warehousing services income rose 44% to ₹2,212 Cr. Including finance and other income of ₹418 Cr, Instakart’s total income fell 3.9% to ₹13,612 Cr in the year under review. Founded in 2009 by Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal as an in-house logistics entity within Flipkart, Ekart was spun off as a separate entity in 2016 to support the fulfillment services not only for Flipkart and Myntra but also for D2C brands, online sellers and retailers. As of last year, the company claimed to be operating more than 7,000 trucks running daily across the length and breadth of the country, 70 fulfilment centres, 80 sortation facilities and 3500 delivery hubs to ensure timely delivery across 14,000 pin codes. Earlier in July, Ekart opened its pan-India logistics network to MSMEs, D2C brands, FMCG companies, and enterprises, allowing external businesses to access the logistics infrastructure used by Flipkart. The logistics arm has already operationalised more than 300 franchise outlets across Surat, Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru, and had plans to expand the network to over 1,000 outlets by the end of 2026. Magnifying Ekart’s Spending Ekart’s total expenses for the fiscal dipped by 13% YoY to ₹13,638 Cr in the year under review, while its costs stood at ₹15,673 Cr in FY25. Here is a closer look at where Ekart spent the highest: Freight, Handling and Servicing Expenses: The spending under this head fell by 17.1% to ₹9,191 Cr in FY25 from ₹11,093 Cr in the previous financial year. Of the overall expenditure, freight costs comprised 67.4%. Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs, which include salaries, provident fund, gratuity, among others, shrunk by 24.9% to ₹958 Cr from ₹1,275 Cr in FY25. Further, it accounted for 7 % of the overall expenses in FY26. Depreciation And Amortisation Expense: These costs increased by 5% to ₹1,456 Cr from ₹1,387 Cr in FY25. title: Rapido Booked By Pune Police Over Alleged Unauthorised Bike-Taxi Operations
content: Pune Police has booked Rapido parent Roppen Transportation Services Pvt Ltd for allegedly running bike-taxi services without the required licence and regulatory approvals, according to an FIR registered at Vishrantwadi police station yesterday. The FIR alleges that the company used its app to facilitate paid passenger rides on two-wheelers registered as non-transport vehicles. The development was first reported by Times of India. Inc42 has reached out to Rapido for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response. The alleged violation came to light when Pune RTO motor vehicle inspector Prasad Govardhan Surwase booked a ride through the Rapido app during an enforcement drive against unauthorised bike-taxi operations. The action came a day after Pune District Collector and Regional Transport Authority (RTA) chairman Jitendra Dudi directed Rapido to immediately suspend bike-taxi operations across Pune district until it obtained an ebike taxi aggregator licence. The FIR also states that the RTO issued the company a notice on Thursday (October 15). The directive followed a meeting with representatives of auto-rickshaw and cab driver unions and aggregators. Dudi warned that continued operations would invite legal action and said the service would not be allowed to resume without a licence. At the same meeting, Dudi directed cab aggregators to submit monthly fare data to the district administration and display RTA-approved fares separately on their apps. The directions followed complaints from auto-rickshaw and cab drivers that aggregators were violating prescribed fare norms. According to Dudi, the existing norms require drivers to receive 80% of the RTA base fare, while passenger fares can range from 50% below the base fare to 1.5 times that amount. He said the administration had received complaints about drivers being underpaid and passengers being charged beyond the permitted range, prompting the monthly reporting requirement. FIR Cites Previous Regulatory Proceedings The complaint also recounts Rapido’s earlier attempts to secure permission to operate in Pune, including the rejection of its licence application in December 2022 and subsequent proceedings before the Bombay High Court and Supreme Court. Rapido challenged the rejection through a writ petition filed in 2022, and the Bombay High Court directed the company to stop operating its app in an order in January 2023. In an order in February 2023, the Supreme Court disposed of the related petitions, allowing the company to approach the High Court to challenge Maharashtra’s January 2023 notification prohibiting the use of non-transport vehicles for aggregation and ride pooling. The complaint also refers to a notice issued by the Transport Commissioner’s Office on April 29, 2025, over alleged unauthorised passenger transport through Rapido’s app. According to the FIR, Rapido applied for an aggregator licence with the Transport Commissioner’s Office in Mumbai on August 11, 2026, but had not received approval at the time of the incident. The FIR further alleges inadequate driver background checks, raising concerns about passenger safety, particularly for women. title: ixigo Swings To ₹63 Cr Profit In Q2, Revenue Rises 13% YoY
content: Online travel aggregator ixigo swung to a consolidated net profit of ₹63.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 from a loss of ₹3.5 Cr a year earlier, helped by an exceptional gain linked to the sale of part of its stake in Freshbus. The company’s operating revenue increased 12.9% to ₹321 Cr during the quarter from ₹284.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. Sequentially, net profit rose 85.2% from ₹34.2 Cr, although operating revenue declined 10% from ₹356.8 Cr. The bottom line received a boost from a ₹40.7 Cr exceptional gain following ixigo’s partial exit from electric bus operator Freshbus . The gain reflects both the stake sale and the remeasurement of its remaining investment. ixigo sold Freshbus shares for ₹36.6 Cr in August, reducing its holding to 8.27% from 25.66%. Consequently, Freshbus ceased to be an associate of the company. Before exceptional items and tax, ixigo posted a profit of ₹31 Cr against a loss of ₹4 Cr in the year-ago quarter. However, this was lower than the ₹44.2 Cr recorded in Q1 FY27. Other income increased to ₹22.1 Cr from ₹5.2 Cr a year earlier, taking total income to ₹343 Cr from ₹289.4 Cr. Total expenses grew 6% to ₹309.5 Cr from ₹291.9 Cr. EBITDA rose to ₹40.1 Cr from ₹1.5 Cr. However, adjusted EBITDA declined 17.2% to ₹23.6 Cr from ₹28.5 Cr, with the corresponding margin narrowing to 7.3% from 10%. The year-ago quarter included a one-off ESOP expense of ₹26.9 Cr. ixigo earns revenue through train, bus, flight, and hotel bookings, alongside value-added services and advertising. Its overall gross transaction value (GTV) grew 22% YoY to ₹5,304.5 Cr. ixigo Bets On Hotels & AI ixigo disclosed hotels as a separate operating segment for the first time in Q2 FY27. Hotel GTV increased 158.7% to ₹111.3 Cr from ₹43 Cr a year earlier. “We continue to invest in hotels and AI as key drivers of our long-term growth,” group CEO Aloke Bajpai, group co-CEO Rajnish Kumar, and group CFO Saurabh Devendra Singh said in a joint statement. The hotel segment’s operating revenue increased to ₹8.1 Cr from ₹1.3 Cr. The business recorded a gross take rate of 12.04%, the highest among ixigo’s segments. However, its contribution loss widened to ₹1.2 Cr from ₹71 Lakh a year earlier, although it narrowed from ₹5.7 Cr in Q1 FY27. The hotel business earns revenue through commissions and advertising. Bookings crossed 4.7 Lakh room nights during the quarter, up 295%, with over 86% of bookings coming from ixigo’s existing users. Its inventory covered more than 70,000 properties, including over 12,000 directly contracted properties across 1,100 towns. The strategy builds on ixigo’s existing train, bus, and flight user base to drive hotel bookings . The company said it continued to invest in hotel supply, product, and customer experience. ixigo also expanded the business through its acquisition of a majority stake in Brevistay . It acquired a 54.66% stake for ₹65.7 Cr, including non-compete fees, and consolidated Brevistay’s financial results from July 1, 2026. On AI adoption, the company said autonomous agents handled 82% of voice queries and 94% of chat queries during the quarter, resolving 43 Lakh queries in total. Train, Bus Growth Offsets Flight Revenue Decline Train remained ixigo’s largest revenue-generating segment, with operating revenue increasing 16.4% to ₹149.1 Cr from ₹128.1 Cr. Train GTV grew 5.4% to ₹2,255.5 Cr from ₹2,140.2 Cr, the slowest growth among its three core ticketing businesses. Contribution profit increased 28.8% to ₹47.2 Cr from ₹36.7 Cr. Meanwhile, flights recorded the sharpest GTV growth among the three businesses. Flight GTV increased 37.2% YoY to ₹2,184.3 Cr, while passenger segments booked grew 8% to about 26 Lakh. However, flight revenue declined 7.5% to ₹82.7 Cr from ₹89.4 Cr, while contribution profit fell 9.8% to ₹35.7 Cr from ₹39.6 Cr. The segment’s gross take rate fell to 7% from 9.38%, indicating lower gross ticketing revenue relative to booking value. However, flight revenue declined 7.5% to ₹82.7 Cr from ₹89.4 Cr, while contribution profit fell 9.8% to ₹35.7 Cr from ₹39.6 Cr. The segment’s gross take rate fell to 7% from 9.38%, indicating lower gross ticketing revenue relative to booking value. Bus bookings delivered growth across transaction value, passenger segments, and revenue. GTV increased 31.6% to ₹752.7 Cr from ₹571.9 Cr, while passenger segments booked grew 28% to about 77 Lakh. Bus operating revenue increased 23.8% YoY to ₹81 Cr, while contribution profit rose 26.6% to ₹43.1 Cr. The company attributed growth in intercity bus demand partly to higher airfares and limited availability of confirmed train tickets, alongside investments in customer experience and supply expansion. Shares of ixigo ended yesterday’s trade 4.34% higher at ₹144.35 on the BSE. The post ixigo Swings To ₹63 Cr Profit In Q2, Revenue Rises 13% YoY appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: Burma Burma Parent Files DRHP For IPO With ₹150 Cr Fresh Issue
content: Hunger Pangs, the parent of restaurant chain Burma Burma, has filed its DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.8 Cr shares. Cofounders and promoters Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer will offload up to 60 Lakh shares each through the OFS. Other selling shareholders include Bbigplas Poly, Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund, Venture Catalysts Angel Growth Fund, and an LV Angel Fund scheme. Burma Burma plans to use ₹117.29 Cr from its fresh issue to open 27 company-owned restaurants over FY28 and FY29, expanding in existing markets and entering new Tier I and Tier II cities. The company expects to open 12 outlets in FY28 and 15 in FY29, with the funds covering civil and interior work, kitchen equipment and other setup costs. While no IPO-funded restaurant is expected to begin operations in FY27, the company has earmarked ₹10 Cr that year for advance payments towards fit-outs and other preparatory expenses. It plans to deploy ₹54.63 Cr in FY28 and ₹52.66 Cr in FY29. Burma Burma has identified locations for five outlets in Bengaluru, Surat, Jaipur, Kolkata and Delhi, and signed letters of intent for the sites. Locations for the remaining restaurants are yet to be finalised. The remaining net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, capped at 25% of the gross proceeds. The development comes months after Burma Burma raised ₹38 Cr at a valuation of ₹500 Cr, to expand its footprint into new cities. It has raised over $11 Mn to date from the likes of Negen Capital, Endurance Capital, Coheron Wealth, among others. Founded in 2013, Hunger Pangs opened its first Burma Burma restaurant in Mumbai in 2014. The chain serves vegetarian Burmese cuisine and operates in the premium casual dining segment. As of July 31, it operated 22 restaurants across nine cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Delhi NCR, alongside a delivery kitchen in Mumbai. Burma Burma competes in the broader Asian dining segment with restaurant chains such as Mainland China, Mamagoto, Yum Yum Cha, and Berco’s. Beyond Burma Burma, the company has conceptualised a premium casual dining chain of Japanese restaurants and noodle shops. The proposed brand remains under research and development. Revenue Grows, But FY26 Loss Widens On the financial front, Hunger Pangs’ operating revenue rose 46.6% to ₹155.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹106.1 Cr in FY25. However, its net loss widened to ₹15.4 Cr from ₹50.5 Lakh a year earlier, as expenses grew faster than revenue. Total expenses increased 61.8% to ₹175.8 Cr from ₹108.7 Cr in FY25. EBITDA grew 20.2% to ₹25.7 Cr from ₹21.4 Cr. However, EBITDA margin contracted to 16.5% from 20.1%. During FY26, the company expanded its restaurant network from 12 to 21 outlets, taking its seating capacity to 1,991 from 1,082. However, the average bill value declined to ₹2,400 from ₹2,560. For Q1 FY27, Hunger Pangs reported operating revenue of ₹53.7 Cr and EBITDA of ₹11.4 Cr, translating into an EBITDA margin of 21.3%. It posted a net profit of ₹1.1 Cr during the quarter, supported by a ₹2 Cr deferred tax credit. Before tax, the company recorded a loss of ₹89 Lakh. title: Enterprise AI Startup RapidCanvas Nets $29 Mn To Expand GTM Teams
content: Enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 Mn (about ₹280 Cr) in its Series B funding round led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India. The round also saw participation from new ventures Hitachi Ventures, along with existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures. RapidCanvas will use the proceeds to expand its go-to-market teams and field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil. It will also invest in all three products — deepening the Enterprise Context Engine, expanding the skills library behind the Visual Development Canvas, and strengthening governance in the Operational Harness. Founded in 2021 by Rahul Pangam and Uttam Phalnikar, RapidCanvas is an agentic AI startup that helps enterprises build and deploy AI applications as well as oversee their performance. RapidCanvas claims that its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has grown 8X over the past six quarters. So far, in 2026, more than 75 enterprises across manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure have made 1.4 Mn AI-led decisions using applications built on its platform. RapidCanvas follows a subscription-based business model and targets large enterprises that have AI budgets but lack the in-house expertise to move beyond pilot projects. It claims that its platform is “trusted” by companies like PayPal, TresVista, Yale Appliances, Orion, Treetech, among others. “Vibe coding has made it easy to start building with AI. Getting AI into production reliably and safely still remains the biggest gap. Our growth over the past six quarters is evidence that AI in enterprises is moving beyond pilots into production and real operations,” said cofounder and CEO Pangam. Enterprise AI Draws Investor Interest RapidCanvas’ fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in enterprise tech startups helping businesses deploy AI across their operations. Yesterday, enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raised $5 Mn in a seed round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures. A day earlier, Parallel Loop secured $6.6 Mn in a seed round led by 3one4 Capital to help businesses integrate AI into their existing systems and workflows. The trend is also reflected in funding data for the Indian AI ecosystem. According to Inc42’s Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026, AI startup funding surged 265% YoY to $438 Mn in the September quarter. Investor sentiment, however, suggests that capital is not flowing indiscriminately across the AI stack. Inc42’s Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, based on responses from more than 85 institutional investors, found that 63% of investors see some degree of froth in Indian AI startup valuations. About half of those who see froth expect a correction within the next 18 months, while another 31% believe valuations are elevated but supported by real revenue. The survey also points to a preference for AI applications that address specific industry needs. Vertical AI applications across sectors such as BFSI, healthcare, defence and agriculture emerged as the leading choice, with 39% of investors expecting them to capture the most value over the next five years. AI hardware and semiconductors followed at 23%, while AI-led IT and business services accounted for 18%. title: E2E Networks Swings To ₹73 Cr Profit In Q2, Revenue Jumps 411% YoY
content: Cloud infrastructure company E2E Networks’ operating revenue jumped 411% to ₹223.8 Cr in the second quarter of FY27 from ₹43.8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. The company posted a consolidated net profit of ₹72.7 Cr during the quarter under review, reversing a net loss of ₹13.5 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue increased 42.7% from ₹156.8 Cr, while net profit rose 65.7% from ₹43.9 Cr. Including other income of ₹9.9 Cr, total income stood at ₹233.7 Cr, compared with ₹52.1 Cr in the September quarter of FY26 and ₹168.2 Cr in the preceding quarter. The company attributed Q2 growth to contributions from Blackwell GPUs, better utilisation, and higher average realisation across its GPU fleet. During the quarter, E2E also signed a multi-year cloud GPU contract worth ₹1,000 Cr with an undisclosed sovereign AI company for NVIDIA Blackwell cloud GPUs and allied services. Speaking on the earnings call, MD Tarun Dua said the contract runs through June 2029 and covers existing B200 capacity previously offered on a pay-as-you-go basis. He added that the company’s existing flagship Blackwell capacity will be fully utilised under the contract. E2E expects to complete another deployment of 1,024 B200 GPUs during the December quarter, Dua said. However, management declined to provide revenue or capital expenditure guidance. Founded in 2009 by Tarun Dua, E2E Networks is an AI-focused cloud provider offering GPU computing infrastructure, AI/ML cloud services, and managed hosting. It positions itself as a domestic alternative to global hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud for AI workloads. Its offerings include B200, H200, and H100 GPU infrastructure. CFO Nitin Jain said customers under the IndiaAI Mission accounted for roughly 13-15% of quarterly revenue, while international customers contributed around 20-25%. Management cautioned that these proportions could vary significantly between quarters. Total expenses increased 93.4% to ₹136.6 Cr from ₹70.6 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, expenditure rose 24.7% from ₹109.6 Cr. The company recorded an EBITDA of ₹171.5 Cr, with its margin increasing to 76.6% from 41.1% in Q2 FY26. On the earnings call, Dua said the company sees EBITDA margins of 70% or more over the medium to long term. Dua said E2E is investing in its AI platforms and retaining some GPU capacity for internal research and product development. The company also added a chief revenue officer, a field CTO, and a founders’ office team during the quarter. Alongside its Q2 disclosures, E2E announced the appointment of Crane Venture Partners’ MD Anandamoy Roychowdhary as its strategic advisor. It also appointed Krishnan Mahesh, a nominee of Larsen & Toubro, as an additional non-executive, non-independent director, subject to shareholder approval. E2E Networks listed on NSE’s SME platform, NSE Emerge, in 2018 before migrating to the NSE mainboard in 2022. In June this year, it took the direct listing route to debut on the BSE mainboard . The listing involved no fresh capital raise or issuance of new shares, with existing shares becoming tradeable on the BSE. Shares of E2E Networks ended today’s trading session 2.41% lower at ₹693.7 apiece on the BSE.
