title: Meet The Most Active Startup Investors Of Q3 2026
content: India’s startup funding market remained selective in the third quarter of 2026, with investors backing fewer startups even as the overall capital deployed saw a modest uptick. Indian startups raised $2.2 Bn in Q3 2026, up 5% from $2.1 Bn in the year-ago quarter, despite the number of funding deals falling 13% to 210. The pool of active investors also shrank 24% YoY to 511 from 676, pointing to a more concentrated funding environment. The trend was particularly visible in the early-stage ecosystem, where investors became more discerning about the startups they backed. At the same time, venture debt continued to be the most prominent source of capital, with debt firms bagging the top most active investors spot this quarter as well. Stride Ventures led the overall investor leaderboard with 38 deals, followed by Alteria Capital with 31. The duo have maintained this lead throughout 2026. Among equity investors, 3one4 Capital topped the list with 19 investments, followed by Rainmatter with 16, IvyCap Ventures with 15 and Antler with 14. With the funding market becoming more selective, these investors stood out for the breadth and consistency of their deployment during the quarter. With that, here’s a look at the most active startup investors of Q3 2026. Stride Ventures The venture debt firm continued to be the most active startup investor in Q3 2026, backing 38 startups during the quarter. Its notable investments included Branch, FreshToHome and GIVA, among others. The firm has been expanding its global presence and currently manages seven debt funds across India, the GCC, the UK and Europe. It is also planning to deploy $1 Bn across global credit markets over the next few years. The firm counts 16 unicorns among its 220+ portfolio companies, including Zetwerk, Udaan, Upstox, Ola Electric and Perfios. Alteria Capital The firm continued to be the second most active investor this quarter after closing 48 deals in the first half of the year. In the September quarter, Alteria closed 31 deals backing startups like Curefoods, Ultrahuman, Yubi, River Mobility and Miraggio, among others. The Mumbai-headquartered firm is known for backing early to growth stage startups across sectors like foodtech, agritech, fintech, deeptech, EV and retail. Alteria Capital manages four funds and has deployed more than $750 Mn to date. The firm has over $550 Mn in assets under management and has backed more than 15 unicorns, including Zepto, BharatPe, Mensa Brands and Spinny. Google Google emerged as the third most active investor in Q3 2026, backing 20 startups via its Google for Startups Accelerator: India 2026 programme. Announced in July, the 2026 cohort comprises 20 AI-first startups selected from nearly 2,500 applications. The startups completed an in-person bootcamp at Google’s Bengaluru campus. As part of the programme, Google will work with the selected startups to refine their products, optimise their technology architecture and prepare them for scaled deployment. Later in September, the company also selected four Indian startups — Terrastack, Varaha Climate, Farmers for Forests and Climitra Carbon — for its debut AI focused accelerator ‘Google DeepMind Accelerator: AI for the Planet (APAC)’. The accelerator aims to address urgent environmental challenges using AI. 3one4 Capital Early-stage venture capital firm 3one4 Capital backed 19 startups during Q3 2026, including Elixir Foods, Smalle and Unbox Robotics. The early-stage focused VC also completely exited EV startup Yulu via a secondary transaction as part of its $93 Mn Series C round which was led by GEF Capital Partners Since inception, 3one4 Capital has invested in more than 110 startups including Licious, DarwinBox, Open, Kuku FM, Jupiter, BetterPlace and Tracxn. As of now, the firm is gearing up to launch its fifth fund, with a target corpus of $225 Mn, 3one4 Capital IFSC – Fund V . The corpus will primarily target startups operating in sectors like AI and SaaS, enterprise and manufacturing automation, fintech, deeptech and consumer internet. Rainmatter Zerodha’s startup investment arm Rainmatter closed 16 deals in Q3 2026. Its notable investments during the quarter included Arboreal, Econovus, Minimac, Quanfluence and SolarSquare. Rainmatter operates as a “perennial” fund using Zerodha’s own capital, allowing it to take a long-term approach to its investments. While it initially focused on fintech, the firm has expanded into areas such as climate tech, D2C and healthtech. The Zerodha-backed investor is increasingly betting on engineering-heavy businesses developing indigenous IP, components and systems upstream of manufacturing. Since its inception in 2016, Rainmatter has built a portfolio of around 160 investments and manages assets worth more than ₹1,500 Cr. Its portfolio includes smallcase, Ultrahuman, The Whole Truth Foods, GalaxEye and Lissun, among others. IvyCap Ventures The VC firm backed 15 startups in Q3 2026, including BatX Energies, Blitz, BotSync, Celcius Logistics and SwitchOn. The firm currently manages more than $650 Mn in assets and has a portfolio of over 65 startups. The investment mix reflects the VC’s focus on tech-led businesses solving problems across India’s physical and consumer economy, rather than a concentration in a single sector. Its portfolio spans deeptech, enterprise technology, healthtech, consumertech, fintech and emerging areas such as EVs and agritech. InnoVen Capital The venture debt firm backed 14 startups in Q3 2026, including the likes of BharatPe, Enerzolve, Infinite Uptime, NuPlayAI and QPi, among others. The firm typically backs startups that have already raised equity and are looking to extend their runway or support growth and has backed more than 200 startups. Meanwhile, its portfolio across Asia includes more than 420 companies. Across markets, the firm has invested more than $1.9 Bn through over 770 debt transactions and counts more than 50 unicorns among its portfolio companies. Its India portfolio includes Swiggy, OYO, Myntra, boAt and Cars24. Antler Global early-stage venture capital firm Antler backed 14 startups in Q3 2026, including Green Aero, Mandrake, Navana, ProLearn and Rovia. Founded in Singapore in 2017, Antler is now present across more than 25 cities and has made over 2,000 investments globally. The firm launched its India operations in 2020, starting with a programme in Bengaluru. In 2023, Antler India closed commitments of ₹500 Cr for its maiden pre-seed fund and was targeting a final close of ₹600 Cr. Antler India typically invests at the idea-to-pre-seed stage, with initial cheques ranging between $200K and $400K. It has backed more than 115 startups through its India fund, including Armory, HouseEazy, Dodo Payments, Inspecity and Green Aero Propulsion. AJVC Early-stage venture capital firm A Junior VC (AJVC) backed 13 startups in Q3 2026, including Alchemic, Bejan, Dialflo and MoroMaa. Founded by Aviral Bhatnagar, AJVC initially launched with a ₹100 Cr fund. The firm later raised ₹165 Cr for its maiden fund against an initial target of ₹100 Cr. The firm is looking to back 80-90 startups through the fund and plans to invest in another 60-70 ventures by early 2028. Typically, AJVC invests about ₹1.5 Cr per startup for a 9% stake. Finvolve Finvolve participated in 13 investment deals in Q3 2026, backing early-stage startups such as Evigway, Kepler Aerospace and Rezlytix. Incorporated in 2022, the firm focuses on startups across sectors such as dronetech, spacetech, clean energy, mobility, circular economy and social impact, as well as businesses leveraging ONDC. To date, Finvolve has made more than 40 investments across deeptech, spacetech, clean energy and fintech. Its portfolio includes Droom, Matter, IG Defence, Recur Club and Sunfox. title: Flipkart Acquires Minority Stake In Travel Tech Startup TravClan To Scale Offerings
content: Walmart-owned Flipkart picked up a minority stake in Delhi-based B2B travel tech startup TravClan to bolster its international travel offerings, expand holiday packages offered by subsidiaries Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel as well as enhancing on-ground support across. The ecommerce giant also aims to leverage the partnership to expand its own curated international leisure offerings by tapping into TravClan’s technology and partner network. On the other side of the table, the fresh capital infusion will support TravClan’s team expansion in business development, engineering, and destination operations, as well as allow for further investments in global supply, technology, and destination expansion. “Travellers today are looking for more than a flight or hotel booking. They want a holiday that is curated around their interests and supported throughout the journey. TravClan’s supplier network and destination capabilities will help us build that experience across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel,” said Nishant Verman, Flipkart’s SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships. Founded by Arun Bagaria, Chirag Agrawal, and Ashish Thapliyal in 2018, TravClan assists travel agents to build and grow online businesses. It works with over 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real-time packages, hotels, and activities. The startup’s cap table also includes angel investors like Cars24 cofounders Vikram Chopra and Mehul Agrawal and Trip.com’s Travis Katz , as well as institutional investors like Leo Capital. Flipkart’s Diversification Push For Flipkart, the travel tech investment adds on to its push to build out its other business verticals beyond its flagship ecommerce platform. While the company has been eyeing new entries in the food delivery and the event ticketing industry, it has been aggressively doubling down on its quick commerce arm, Flipkart Minutes. Ahead of its annual Big Billion Days, the ecommerce giant announced that it has expanded its dark store network to nearly 1,200 Flipkart Minutes microfulfillment centres across 150-plus cities. The company is now expected to add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027 or the Big Billion Days sale of 2027. In recent years, it has also expanded its in-house Flipkart Travel beyond flight booking services into bus bookings and hotel bookings . Cleartrip, an online travel aggregator which Flipkart acquired in 2021, also later expanded into corporate travel . Besides, Flipkart made some additional investments in AI startups last week. Its investment arm Flipkart Ventures backed Alive, an AI-powered platform for live consumer experiences, and Keploy, a native-AI software testing platform. To date, Flipkart has made over 20 startup investments via Flipkart Ventures across AI, consumer internet, fintech, e-commerce adjacencies and logistics tech. It claims to support portfolio ventures with strategic mentorship, operational expertise and access to its ecosystem in order to help them scale, besides the capital they get. title: [Update] Snapdeal Parent AceVector Ends Market Debut 18.5% Below Issue Price
content: Update | October 5, 2026 16:40 IST Snapdeal parent AceVector’s shares closed their maiden trading session at ₹26.10 on the BSE, 18.4% below the issue price of ₹32 and 7.8% below the listing price of ₹28.30. The stock recovered from an intraday low of ₹23.40. On the NSE, the stock ended at ₹26.08, down 18.5% from the issue price and 7.9% from its listing price of ₹28.32. It touched an intraday low of ₹23.37. The company ended the session with a market capitalisation of ₹1,420.3 Cr (about $147.4 Mn) on the BSE. Original | October 5, 2026 10:00 IST Snapdeal parent AceVector made a weak stock market debut, listing at ₹28.30 on the BSE, an 11.6% discount to its issue price of ₹32 per share. On the NSE, the stock debuted at ₹28.32, an 11.5% discount to the IPO price. At its BSE listing price, AceVector commanded a market capitalisation of ₹1,540.1 Cr (about $161 Mn), down from its IPO valuation of ₹1,741.4 Cr (about $181.7 Mn). AceVector had set the IPO price band at ₹30-₹32 per share. The company’s ₹420 Cr IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹287 Cr and an OFS of up to 4.16 Cr shares, worth ₹133 Cr at the issue price. The IPO closed with an oversubscription of 4.93X. The issue received bids for 36.61 Cr shares against 7.42 Cr shares on offer. The OFS delivered sharply different outcomes for selling shareholders. SoftBank’s Starfish I Pte Ltd received ₹88.3 Cr from the sale of 2.76 Cr shares, but recovered just 0.08X its acquisition cost on those shares. Individual investor Kenneth Stuart Glass, meanwhile, booked a 5.4X return multiple on his ₹4.2 Cr share sale. Ahead of the IPO, AceVector raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors. The only two mutual funds which participated were Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund. AceVector has earmarked ₹132 Cr from the fresh issue proceeds for Snapdeal’s marketing and business promotion, and ₹50 Cr for technology infrastructure. The remaining proceeds will fund acquisitions and general corporate purposes. Founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, the business began as Snapdeal and adopted the AceVector identity in 2022. Besides the marketplace, the group’s businesses include listed ecommerce SaaS company Unicommerce and consumer brands business Stellaro Brands. Snapdeal now focuses on value ecommerce, with fashion contributing more than 60% of its business. Around 84% of its customers come from non-metro geographies. Ahead of the IPO, Bahl told Inc42 that the marketplace would prioritise volume growth, expansion within its existing categories, and better merchandising. However, Snapdeal faces a wide gap in scale with rival Meesho , which clocked net merchandise value of ₹41,560 Cr in FY26, about 38 times Snapdeal’s ₹1,093.1 Cr. On the financial front, AceVector’s restated net loss narrowed nearly 64% to ₹45.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹126.3 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue rose 29.2% to ₹510.3 Cr from ₹395 Cr. title: Razorpay Partners With OpenAI To Help Indian Brands Advertise On ChatGPT
content: IPO-bound Razorpay announced today that it has deepened its partnership with AI major OpenAI to help Indian brands advertise on ChatGPT. Under the partnership, the company’s growth marketing platform, Razorpay Engage, will enable brands to prepare product catalogues, launch and manage campaigns on ChatGPT Ads. Brands onboarded by Razorpay include Tanishq, Fastrack, Traya, Tata Neu, Rivaah by Tanishq, Shaadi.com, Axis Max Life, Palmonas and Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies (NMIMS). Razorpay Engage To Become ChatGPT Ads Layer Razorpay Engage will provide the technology and operational infrastructure for businesses looking to get started with ChatGPT Ads. Its offering will include assessing catalogue readiness, improving and structuring product feeds, creating and managing campaigns, and measuring and optimising campaign performance. The platform will also use an AI agent built around ChatGPT Ads best practices to help create and manage campaigns across different contexts where consumers may encounter a brand’s products. The agent will monitor campaign performance and make ongoing adjustments, while Razorpay’s team will provide human oversight where required. “The way people discover products is changing. The next customer may not search for a product or scroll through an ad; they may simply ask an AI assistant for help deciding what to buy. For businesses, we believe that opens up an entirely new moment to be discovered,” Razorpay COO Rahul Kothari said. The Broader Context Behind OpenAI-Razorpay Partnership The partnership comes as consumer discovery of brands is shifting from traditional keyword-based searches on engines to conversational interactions with AI chatbots. An early trend of users describing what they are looking for to an AI bot, comparing options and refine their choices via subsequent conversations is emerging at the moment. As this trend gains more footing, ChatGPT started rolling out ads on ChatGPT in India , with the initial rollout covering logged-in adults on the Free and Go plans at the end of August. Ad agencies WPP and Omnicom are OpenAI’s first agency partners in India. For brands, this creates a new channel where products need to be structured and represented with sufficient information and context to surface across different consumer queries. Razorpay said managing this process manually at scale can be challenging. The advertising push builds on Razorpay’s earlier efforts to turn ChatGPT into a commerce channel. The fintech company has been working with OpenAI and NPCI on infrastructure that allows merchants to create ChatGPT-native storefronts, sync product catalogues and eventually complete purchases within the chat interface. In August, Razorpay said it was working with around 50 brands and several ecommerce marketplaces on agentic-commerce pilots. The company has also earlier said that its technology can reduce the time required for a Shopify merchant to set up a ChatGPT storefront from around eight to 10 weeks to roughly 30 minutes by automating catalogue syncing and the submission process. The broader proposition is that merchants need more than visibility on AI platforms: they also need structured catalogues, storefronts and payment infrastructure that can work inside conversational interfaces. Razorpay has been building these layers as it seeks to establish itself as an infrastructure provider for AI-led commerce. This also marks a continuation of Razorpay’s partnership with OpenAI and NPCI around agentic payments. The company has been experimenting with UPI Circle and UPI Reserve Pay to enable purchases within ChatGPT, while keeping payment credentials away from the AI model and requiring user consent for transactions. Razorpay’s push comes as other payment companies, including Cashfree and Pine Labs, are also building infrastructure for agentic commerce, suggesting that payment providers see the AI interface as a potential new layer between consumers and merchants rather than simply another checkout channel. The partnership also marks another step in Razorpay’s expansion beyond its core payments business. Razorpay was founded in 2014 by IIT Roorkee alumni Shashank Kumar and Harshil Mathur and has expanded from payments into a broader suite of business and banking solutions. Razorpay launched Engage in 2023 as a full-stack growth marketing platform, offering businesses customer acquisition, retention and engagement tools. The platform provides personalised incentives, gift cards and targeted rewards across an inventory of more than 5,000 options. Its AI push, meanwhile, extends beyond commerce and advertising. In August, Razorpay launched Vulcan , a proprietary AI foundation model designed to improve payment success, fraud detection and transaction routing, underlining the company’s broader attempt to build AI into its payments infrastructure. Razorpay has also been developing Agent Studio, its platform for deploying task-specific AI agents for businesses. Around 200 businesses were using the platform in beta as of August, with use cases including reconciliation, abandoned-cart recovery, subscription recovery and finance operations. The company has previously described this as a broader “distribution layer” across different agentic touchpoints, including merchant websites, independent agent platforms and large language model platforms, rather than a bet solely on ChatGPT. The startup, which has raised over $800 M from investors like Tiger Global, Y Combinator, Lightspeed, is gearing up for a public markets debut soon. title: ideaForge Founder Ankit Mehta Pledges 2.8 Lakh Shares For “Personal Requirements”
content: Dronetech company ideaForge Technology promoter and CEO Ankit Mehta has pledged 2.8 Lakh shares — 0.56% of the company’s total share capital — for “personal financial requirements.” According to an exchange filing dated October 2, Mehta created the pledge on September 28 in favour of Infina Finance Pvt Ltd. Following the pledge, the total number of encumbered shares held by Infina increased to 6.50 Lakh, representing 1.30% of ideaForge’s share capital. As per the opening price of ideaForge at BSE today, Mehta pledged shares worth ₹20.56 Cr. The CEO held 36.87 Lakh shares, or 7.42% of ideaForge’s share capital, prior to the fresh pledge. The newly pledged shares represent 2.23% of promoter holding. The pledge comes at a time when ideaForge’s shares are trading on an upward trajectory. The shares have gained about 54% on a year-to-date basis. On the financial front, the drone maker reported a net loss of ₹2.3 Cr in Q1 FY27, reversing the ₹61 Cr profit recorded in Q4 FY26. Meanwhile, its operating revenue rose 436% YoY to ₹68.6 Cr, although it declined 51% sequentially from ₹141 Cr in the March quarter. In the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year, ideaForge raised ₹500 Cr through a QIP in July by allotting around 62.89 Lakh shares to qualified institutional buyers at ₹795 apiece. Of the proceeds, around ₹165 Cr was earmarked for working capital, ₹120 Cr for debt repayment or prepayment and ₹90 Cr for product development. Recently, the listed company received a ₹109.2 Cr GST demand and penalty order over alleged tax underpayment for January 2022 to March 2024. Shares of ideaForge were trading -2.97% lower at ₹712.50 as of 13:40 IST. The post ideaForge Founder Ankit Mehta Pledges 2.8 Lakh Shares For “Personal Requirements” appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: PhysicsWallah To Sell ₹96 Cr Loan Portfolio To Auxilo Amid Lending Retreat
content: Edtech major PhysicsWallah’s wholly owned subsidiary FinZ Finance has agreed to sell a ₹95.79 Cr loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve, taking forward the company’s retreat from direct student lending announced four months ago. FinZ signed the deed of assignment on Saturday (October 3), with the transition of the loans and associated borrowers expected to conclude within 60 days, PhysicsWallah said in an exchange filing yesterday. The portfolio represents a substantial portion of FinZ’s loan book. The filing also pegged the consideration for the transaction at ₹95.79 Cr. “As the principal business activity of FinZ Finance is lending, the proposed transaction constitutes a substantial reduction in its lending operations and is expected to result in partial/piecemeal closure of its lending operations,” the company said. PhysicsWallah said the sale forms part of a broader strategic realignment to optimise capital allocation and focus on its core business. Lending would instead be facilitated through established, regulated third-party NBFCs to reduce balance sheet exposure and credit risks. Founded in 2017, Mumbai-based Auxilo Finserve is an RBI-registered NBFC that provides education loans and financing to students and other stakeholders in the education sector. Unwinding The Lending Push The transaction follows PhysicsWallah’s decision in June to reverse its direct student lending strategy , shortly after approving a ₹120 Cr capital infusion into FinZ Finance in May. The proposed investment put pressure on the company’s shares and raised concerns about its capital allocation priorities. Announcing the reversal, cofounder Prateek Maheshwari said feedback from partners indicated that the company should focus on its education business and leave lending to NBFCs with established underwriting capabilities. Under the revised model, the edtech company would operate as a technology platform connecting students with lending partners, with financing tailored to their learning lifecycle and academic progress. It said this would improve affordability and accessibility while making financing more scalable and better integrated into its student ecosystem. At the time, PhysicsWallah said FinZ’s future strategic direction would be decided subsequently, subject to board and regulatory approvals. FinZ commenced business operations in February 2026, according to the latest filing. It reported negligible operating revenue and ₹1.35 Cr in other income in FY26, taking its total income to ₹1.35 Cr, or 0.04% of PhysicsWallah’s total income. Its net worth stood at ₹60.3 Cr as of March 31, representing 1.18% of PhysicsWallah’s net worth. As Inc42 previously reported , PhysicsWallah’s lending push raised questions about the potential conflict between driving student enrolments and maintaining lending discipline when the same group controls both education and financing. The concerns also reflected the sector’s experience with BYJU’S, whose use of third-party loans to finance courses drew allegations of mis-selling and coercive recovery practices. Meanwhile, PhysicsWallah’s operating revenue rose 24.4% to ₹1,054 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹847.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its net loss narrowed 30.5% to ₹88.3 Cr from ₹127 Cr in Q1 FY26. However, the loss widened 27.8% from ₹69.1 Cr in the preceding quarter. Shares of PhysicsWallah were trading 6.12% higher at ₹127.50 on the BSE at 13:42 IST. title: Exclusive: Leverage Edu Eyes ₹500 Cr Pre-IPO Funding, Targets ₹600 Cr Revenue In FY27
content: IPO-bound study abroad platform Leverage Edu is targeting ₹600 Cr in revenue in FY27, up over 60% from the ₹372 Cr it reported in FY26, sources told Inc42. The startup’s management wants to reach this revenue milestone before taking it public. Alongside its listing preparations, Leverage Edu is exploring a ₹500 Cr pre-IPO funding round to bring a large private equity firm onto its cap table. The startup has held talks with a couple of global PE firms and is expected to close the round soon, the sources said. “Akshay has committed to the board that the company will file DRHP by the end of next year. He is currently out in the market to finalise investment bankers for the IPO,” one of the sources said, referring to founder and CEO Akshay Chaturvedi. Leverage Edu did not respond to Inc42’s questions till the time of publication. Preparing For A Public Listing Inc42 earlier exclusively reported that the startup is planning a ₹2,000–3,000 Cr IPO , comprising a fresh issue of shares and an OFS. The split between the two components is yet to be decided. The startup is targeting a valuation of over $900 Mn for the IPO. Pitch decks prepared by investment bankers and accessed by Inc42 position Leverage Edu alongside platform businesses such as Zomato, ixigo, and Shadowfax, with expectations of similar valuation multiples. It turned EBITDA profitable in FY26, posting an EBITDA of ₹9.5 Cr, according to the sources. Meanwhile, Leverage Edu has been expanding its international presence. In July, Inc42 reported that the startup entered South America through the acquisition of Brazil-based international education company Mundus Agency . Besides its flagship app, it offers courses through the Leverage IELTS and Leverage TOEFL apps. The startup’s services spanning fintech, accommodation, travel, and career support account for 25–33% of its total revenue. It also claimed to have added over 55,000 students in FY26, taking its total customer base to over 1.75 Lakh. title: Bhavish Aggarwal Pledges 4.32% Ola Electric Stake To Fund Rights Issue Subscription
content: Ola Electric founder and CMD Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the electric two-wheeler maker to fund his participation in the company’s proposed rights issue of up to ₹1,000 Cr. In an exchange filing yesterday, the company said the pledge was solely meant to finance Aggarwal’s subscription to the issue and that there were no other pledges outstanding on his securities. “No shares are being sold. The promoter will invest alongside all other shareholders on the same terms,” Ola Electric said. Citing the promoter’s disclosures under SAST regulations, PTI reported that the arrangement involves pledging 20 Cr shares in favour of CTL Trusteeship Limited to secure non-convertible debentures issued by Krutrim Data Centre Pvt Ltd. The report described Krutrim Data Centre as a non-operative promoter group entity owned by Aggarwal, separate from Krutrim SI Designs, which operates the AI and cloud infrastructure businesses. The debenture proceeds will fund Aggarwal’s participation in Ola Electric’s rights issue, it added. Ola Electric’s statement did not disclose the amount raised against the shares or the financing terms. According to the draft letter of offer filed last week, Aggarwal held a 26.52% stake in Ola Electric as of June 30, 2026. The 20 Cr pledged shares represent about 16.3% of that holding. The draft document said Aggarwal has committed to subscribing to his full rights entitlement, subject to provisions allowing him to renounce entitlements in favour of promoter group members or specified investors. He may also subscribe to additional shares or any portion left unsubscribed, subject to minimum public shareholding requirements. The disclosure comes after Ola Electric’s board cleared the rights issue on September 28. The issue is part of a broader ₹1,500 Cr fundraising plan approved by the board on September 5. The company has not announced whether or how it will raise the remaining ₹500 Cr. Ola Electric said it chose the rights issue route to enable participation by eligible retail, institutional, and promoter group shareholders. Debt Repayment, Expansion Drive Fundraise Of the proceeds, the company plans to deploy ₹350 Cr towards repaying or prepaying borrowings of Ola Electric and its material subsidiaries, including accrued interest and applicable prepayment penalties. Another ₹400 Cr is earmarked for organic growth initiatives across its electric mobility and energy storage businesses, including manufacturing, R&D, stores, dealerships, service infrastructure, and sales and marketing. The remaining net proceeds will go towards general corporate purposes. The company expects to deploy the funds during FY27 and FY28. As the shares will be partly paid-up, shareholders will pay a portion on application and the balance through a subsequent call. The draft document envisages completing the first and final call by October 31, 2027, although the board can revise the schedule. The proposed issue follows Ola Electric’s ₹780.2 Cr QIP in June . Of the ₹744.9 Cr net proceeds, it earmarked ₹225 Cr for debt repayment, ₹335 Cr for organic growth initiatives, and ₹184.9 Cr for general corporate purposes. Fundraising Amid Falling Revenue, Market Share The fundraising push comes amid continued pressure on Ola Electric’s business. Its consolidated operating revenue fell 45% to ₹455 Cr in Q1 FY27 from ₹828 Cr in the year-ago quarter, while net loss narrowed 21.5% to ₹336 Cr from ₹428 Cr. For FY26, operating revenue halved to ₹2,253 Cr from ₹4,514 Cr in FY25, while E2W deliveries fell to 1.74 Lakh units from 3.59 Lakh units. More recently, Ola Electric recorded 13,449 registrations in September , down 3.5% MoM, giving it around 6.5% of the E2W market, according to Vahan data as of October 1. The company described FY26 as a “year of structural reset”, during which it rationalised its retail network, cut costs, strengthened service operations, and focused on improving unit economics. It has since opened its first dealer-operated stores across seven states . Last month, it outlined plans to build a network of more than 500 dealerships over the following two quarters, with dealer partners handling local sales and service and company-owned outlets transitioning into product experience centres. Beyond E2Ws, Ola Electric is expanding its battery cell manufacturing and battery energy storage businesses. It also launched the S1Z escooter range in August, powered by its internally developed Bharat Cell LFP technology. At 13:20 IST, Ola Electric’s shares were trading at ₹36.76, down 0.89% from the previous day’s close. title: The Rise Of Bank-Built AI, Weekly Funding Rundown & More
content: Banking’s AI Investment Playbook No longer content with buying AI tools, banks are moving to co-build and invest in AI startups. As partnerships deepen and automation reshapes banking jobs, are financial institutions rewriting the playbook for enterprise innovation? Bankers’ Logic: Across the 50 largest global banks, investments in AI companies have grown at a 21% CAGR since 2023. But why? Financial workflows demand more than a standard software. Banks need systems adapted to their compliance requirements, risks and internal data. An investment or co-development arrangement gives them greater influence over product architecture and roadmap. The Desi Model: Back home, financial institutions are actively backing domain-specific AI platforms. HDFC Bank and Canara Bank have invested in AI startup CoRover, while IDFC FIRST Bank’s partnership with Sarvam aims to develop a “self-improving bank” via frontier research and AI safety. Meanwhile, Bajaj Finance has set aside ₹1,500 Cr to back AI platforms. Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank are also collaborating directly with specialised voice AI startups to build niche operational workflows that are difficult to replicate in-house. Win-Win For All: Banks bring more than capital. They offer access to proprietary data, large customer bases, operational feedback and regulated environments in which AI systems can be tested. For startups, these assets can accelerate product development while providing credibility that is difficult to establish through conventional enterprise sales. The Human Layer: The AI transition within banks is also changing the workforce. Axis Bank reduced its workforce by 3,100 employees in FY26, while other lenders have linked AI-related investments to productivity improvements and slower headcount growth. Yet as AI handles more decisions and workflows, human accountability becomes more and more important. As banks become investors, customers and co-developers, what does it mean for the domestic AI ecosystem? Let’s find out… From The Editor’s Desk Weekly Funding Rundown Indian startups cumulatively managed to secure $233.6 Mn last week, up nearly 15% from $203 Mn raised in the preceding week. However, deal count declined 23.8% week-on-week to 16. Simple Energy emerged as the most funded startup last week. Cleantech topped the funding charts last week and attracted $180 Mn across just one round. Ecommerce yet again led in deal activity, with four startups collectively raising a mere $3.8 Mn. Early stage funding activity remained lukewarm as seed-stage and pre-seed startups raised $3.3 Mn across four deals. Alteria Capital emerged as the most active investor last week, backing three startups. Kuku’s Profitable FY26 The OTT platform reported a profit of ₹182.7 Cr in FY26 against a loss of ₹152.6 Cr in the year ago fiscal. The profitability came on the back of a deferred tax credit of ₹98.2 Cr and operating revenue zooming 6X YoY to ₹1,484.2 Cr. At the operating level, Kuku Technologies swung to an EBITDA profit of ₹82.9 Cr in FY26 from an EBITDA loss of ₹159.8 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, expenses continued to bite and surged 3.5X YoY to ₹1,421.8 Cr in the fiscal under review. The profitable show comes as Kuku is gearing up to list on the bourses. The startup has already received SEBI nod for its likely ₹2,500 Cr IPO, which could potentially value it at ₹15,000 Cr. It has raised over $156 Mn to date. Bearish Week For Startup Stocks Of the 65 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 47 ended last week in the red and fell between 0.08% and 20.1%. The remaining 18 stocks gained between 0.17% and 22.55%. Zappfresh and Aequs emerged as the biggest gainers last week, while Turtlemint and ESDS shed the most. The combined m-cap of 66 new-age tech stocks, including recently listed Moneyview, stood at $153.61 Bn at the end of the last week. The subdued performance unfolded against a weak market backdrop, with FII selling and crude oil concerns weighing on sentiment. Investors will now be looking for RBI’s policy decision, PMI readings and Q2 FY27 earnings for market cues next week. AceVector All Set For Listing The Snapdeal parent is all set to list on the bourses today, bringing mixed gains for some of its early backers. SoftBank-backed Starfish is selling 2.76 Cr shares for about ₹88.3 Cr at a 0.08X return multiple. Nexus Venture Partners will book an average 0.4X multiple on its sold shares. However, individual shareholders like Kenneth Glass and Laurent Bernard Amouyal are sitting on 5.42X and 4.3X gains, respectively. AceVector’s ₹420 Cr public issue comprised a fresh issue worth ₹287 Cr and an OFS of up to 4.16 Cr shares. The issue values the company at about ₹1,741 Cr at the upper end of its ₹30-₹32 IPO price band. Its public issue was oversubscribed 4.93X. Bitchat Goes Offline In India Both Google Play Store and Apple App Store have taken down the decentralised messaging platform following a government directive. Apple said that the takedown order was issued under Section 69A of the IT Act over content deemed illegal in India. Without specifying what content had triggered the takedown order, Apple further noted that beta-testing access via TestFlight has also been blocked. The app would, however, remain available on its App Store outside India. Launched by Twitter founder Jack Dorsey in 2025, Bitchat is a messaging app that enables P2P communication through Bluetooth mesh networks without internet access. The app does not require users to make accounts and has no central identity system. Yet finding skilled blue-collar staff at short notice remains difficult. Factrika is turning this gap into an on-demand workforce platform that matches verified workers with factory shifts in real time. Staffing For Factories: Founded in 2024, Factrika helps manufacturers source, deploy and manage workers by skill, location and shift timing. The startup claims to have so far completed 65,000+ shifts and can deploy workers within two hours of a request. title: Snapdeal Makes It To D-Street, But Where’s The Moat?
content: One of India’s earliest ecommerce marketplaces has finally trotted onto D-Street. After a relatively muted 4.93X subscription to its IPO, Snapdeal’s parent AceVector is all set to make its stock market debut on Monday. AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO, which opened on September 25 and closed on September 29, comprised a fresh issue of ₹287 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of around ₹133 Cr, with shares priced in the ₹30-32 band. The company’s IPO response is a far cry from its once-lofty standing in India’s ecommerce race. At its peak, the company was valued at $6.5 Bn, backed by heavyweight investors, including SoftBank Group, Alibaba Group and Foxconn. Then, as Amazon poured billions into building its India business and Flipkart emerged as a formidable rival, the ecommerce battle grew increasingly intense. Snapdeal eventually stepped away from its ambition of competing across the broader market and shifted its focus to affordable fashion, home and beauty products, catering to shoppers in Tier II and Tier III India looking for low-priced goods rather than premium brands. But is value commerce really working for it? Let’s find out in this edition of Inc42 Markets. How AceVector Makes Money Snapdeal is only one part of AceVector’s portfolio. The company has two other businesses: Unicommerce, an ecommerce enablement software business, and Stellaro Brands, its consumer-brands arm. According to an expert tracking the consumer internet sector, Snapdeal has grown its net merchandise value and customer base of value-conscious shoppers, but its scale remains quite modest compared with larger ecommerce platforms, especially Meesho. The expert added that Snapdeal may not be generating enough revenue per transaction to cover customer acquisition, technology and logistics costs. Unlike an inventory-led retailer, Snapdeal operates an asset-light marketplace. Sellers own and list products, while Snapdeal facilitates discovery, transactions and associated services. It earns money through seller-related marketplace fees, advertising and marketing services, freight and collection fees, and charges for return shipments. This structure limits the need to purchase and hold inventory, but leaves the company dependent on transaction volumes, seller participation and the economics of fulfilling orders. The marketplace revenue rose to ₹293.7 Cr in FY26 from ₹249.9 Cr in FY25. Net merchandise value (NMV), the value of delivered merchandise after excluding cancellations and returns, increased 25.7% to ₹1,093.1 Cr, from ₹869.6 Cr in FY25. In FY24, NMV stood at ₹633.3 Cr, even as marketplace revenue remained relatively flat between FY24 and FY25 before rising in FY26. The gap between NMV and revenue is important. NMV measures the value of merchandise transacted on the platform; it is not the amount Snapdeal earns. In FY26, marketplace revenue was roughly 26.9% of NMV, down from 28.7% in FY25. Meanwhile, marketplace marketing and business promotion expenses climbed to ₹84.4 Cr in FY26, from ₹63.2 Cr in FY25 and ₹58.5 Cr in FY24. The company’s ecommerce enablement arm, Unicommerce, has emerged as a significant growth driver within the group. Its SaaS revenue rose 51.6% to ₹204.3 Cr in FY26 from ₹134.8 Cr in FY25, compared with Snapdeal’s marketplace revenue growth of 17.5% during the same period. The business provides order, inventory and warehouse management software through Uniware, alongside shipping and logistics automation through Shipway and marketing automation through Convertway. Its acquisition of Shipway Technology added to this portfolio, extending its services across more stages of the ecommerce lifecycle. Meanwhile, AceVector’s consumer brands business, housed under Stellaro Brands, remains smaller but expansion-heavy. It operates Rangita, a women’s ethnic wear brand sold online and through an omnichannel retail network. Stellaro’s revenue from operations rose to ₹12.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹11.4 Cr in FY25. What Does Snapdeal Offer Beyond Brand Recall? Snapdeal has been in the game since 2010, one of the early players that helped open the floodgates to online shopping in India. According to Karan Taurani, executive vice president at Elara Capital, Snapdeal has an edge in terms of brand recall. He said the company has remained relevant through multiple changes in its business model, from deal-led discounting to a broader marketplace and, more recently, a value-commerce platform. “Its longevity gives it an established identity among consumers, but that alone may not be enough to sustain growth in a market where customer acquisition, transaction frequency and operational efficiency are increasingly important,” Taurani said. He is of the view that Snapdeal’s focus on value-conscious shoppers does give it a clear customer segment to serve, but it also operates in a crowded market where affordability is not exclusive to one platform. Meesho, which has built a much larger marketplace around value-conscious consumers, is a key example. In FY26, Snapdeal clocked an NMV of ₹1,093.1 Cr, while Meesho’s marketplace raked in ₹41,560 Cr. This is a staggering 38X scale gap. The gap also extends beyond merchandise value to the number of customers and transactions each platform handles. Snapdeal reported 12.16 Mn annual transacting users and 25.98 Mn delivered units in FY26. Meesho reported 264.29 Mn annual transacting users and 1.71 Bn delivered units. Therefore, Snapdeal’s central challenge is scale, even in its value segment. Snapdeal Has AI Tools But Is There A Real Competitive Edge? At a time when Meesho has an extensive technology stack, including AI-led tools, Snapdeal is trying to take steps in a similar direction. Snapdeal recently introduced a multi-solution AI suite aimed at making fashion discovery more personalised, visual and conversational for Indian shoppers. The suite brings together AI-powered recommendations, conversational search, image-based discovery and customer experience tools across the marketplace. According to its RHP, 72.69% of orders in FY26 were placed without users entering a search term. The company attributes this to its recommendation engine and personalised product feeds, which use browsing history, product interactions and other data to tailor the shopping experience. Overall, its tech stack supports processes such as seller onboarding, catalogue ingestion and fraud detection. AI-supported customer service is available through channels including calls, WhatsApp, IVR and in-app support. Snapdeal may have added AI to the shopping cart, but that does not necessarily give it a competitive edge. Recommendation engines, conversational search and AI-powered support are increasingly becoming standard ecommerce features. For Snapdeal, AI is currently an ongoing bet. What it needs to solve immediately is the puzzle of scale. title: Is Apple Pay’s India Entry Too Late?
content: The past fortnight has brought several developments around Apple in India. The iPhone 18 Pro and Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo began shipping, putting the company’s latest hardware in focus. But another development has drawn attention: Apple Pay, a service the company has been talking about bringing to India for more than a decade, is finally here. Apple launched the service in India on September 30, 2026, allowing users to pay at physical stores, within apps and on websites using an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch. In 2016, then CEO Tim Cook during his visit to India said that Apple was looking at bringing Apple Pay to India, and had even met the then ICICI Bank CEO Chanda Kochhar to understand the bank’s views on mobile payments. Ten years later, Apple Pay is finally here, but the payments landscape has changed considerably. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 24.51 Bn transactions wort h ₹29.82 Lakh Cr in August 2026, as per the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). The question is whether Apple can find room in a market where consumers already have several ways to pay. Narrower Than The US Version Apple Pay allows users to add eligible cards to Apple Wallet and authenticate payments through Face ID, Touch ID or their device passcode. At physical stores, they can tap their devices against compatible contactless terminals. Online, they can pay without repeatedly entering card details. The India offering is narrower than the service available in the US, where customers can use cards from a wider range of participating banks and issuers. US users can also access Apple Cash for person-to-person money transfers, subject to eligibility. Apple has not announced a comparable service for India. At launch, Apple Pay supports eligible Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards. RuPay cards and cards from other banks are not supported under the initial rollout. This limits the number of consumers who can use the service, even among iPhone owners. Tarun Pathak of Counterpoint Research said Apple’s entry is late from both a global launch and competition standpoint, but pointed to regulatory requirements and the relatively small size of India’s installed iPhone base as possible reasons for the delay. “Clearance of regulatory and technical roadblocks allowed Apple to hold its standard global architecture when it comes to Apple Pay experience built around NFC card tokenisation, plus the native Apple ecosystem leveraging the security of Face ID, Touch ID, and Apple Watch integration for fast NFC tap-to-pay at POS terminals,” Pathak said. Apple’s approach keeps the payment experience tied to its own devices and security architecture. However, the restricted bank rollout means the company will need to expand its partnerships before the service can reach a wider customer base. UPI Poses A Challenge For Apple Pay UPI’s dominance presents a different challenge for Apple Pay. Unlike markets where card-based payment plays a larger role, India has built a digital payment ecosystem around direct bank-to-bank transfers, with consumers using apps such as PhonePe and Google Pay for everyday transactions. According to the Reserve Bank of India’s Payment System Report, December 2025, UPI accounted for 85.5% of digital transaction volume. This figure underlines how firmly UPI is embedded in India’s payment ecosystem, leaving Apple Pay to build adoption in a market where consumers already have an established way to pay. Apple Pay’s launch in India does not support UPI integration. Its initial use case is therefore centred on consumers who own compatible Apple devices and hold eligible credit cards. With Apple Pay, the company is offering contactless payments, but Apple will need to give users a reason to choose card-based payment through its devices when UPI is already widely available. The availability of tap-to-pay alone may not be enough to change consumer habits. Samsung Wallet already offers NFC-based payments on compatible Galaxy devices, alongside other wallet features. Despite Samsung supporting UPI payments, it has hardly made a dent. An industry insider who has worked in fintech told Inc42 that the service is unlikely to make a major difference to the sector in its current form. “Apple Pay launch is only restricted to Axis Bank, with no UPI integration. Even today Android users are around 90% of the mobile phone users. Apple Pay is just allowing you to save the card and pay via NFC,” the insider said. The insider also pointed to existing options for Android users, saying popular apps such as Phonepe have integrated card-based payment features for Visa and Mastercard users. The source expects some Apple users to adopt the service for high ticket purchases but does not see it as a threat to the fintech industry. The insider also questioned whether Apple would enter UPI, citing NPCI’s transaction data storage requirements and Apple’s policies of not storing transaction details. Can Apple Pay Drive Card Payments? Apple Pay’s entry could give a push to credit card transactions, particularly among iPhone users who prefer using cards for higher value purchases. Amrish Rau, MD and CEO of Pine Labs, had anticipated the service’s India entry before its launch, arguing that it could shift some transactions towards cards as credit card payments and UPI continue to grow. “We do believe Apple Pay will enter the market before the end of this year. What that is going to do is flip and create a spread in terms of how payment transactions will happen. More and more payment transactions will go back to credit cards, as credit cards plus UPI continue to grow in the market,” Rau said during the company’s Q1FY27 earnings discussion. Data from the Reserve Bank of India’s Payment System Report , December 2025 points to the growth in credit card spending. Credit card spending rose to ₹23.2 Lakh Cr in calendar year 2025, up from ₹8.9 Lakh Cr in 2021. Private banks also strengthened their position in the segment, accounting for 71.1% of outstanding credit cards. Debit card usage, meanwhile, has moved in the opposite direction. Transaction volumes fell 67% between CY2021 and CY2025, as consumers increasingly shifted to UPI for everyday payments. The divergence matters for Apple Pay. While UPI has become a common choice for routine transfers and purchases, credit cards continue to serve consumers looking for credit, rewards and payment flexibility. Apple pay could make card payments more convenient by allowing users to tap their devices at compatible terminals instead of carrying a physical card. However, growth in credit card spending does not automatically translate into demand for Apple Pay. Besides, its reach will also depend on how many consumers are willing to change their existing payment habits. For Apple, the immediate opportunity may be to increase the frequency with which existing users pay by card through its devices. Whether that translates into a meaningful shift in India’s payment mix will depend on wider bank support, merchant acceptance and consumer adoption. title: Jack Dorsey’s Bitchat Goes Offline In India, Apple Cites MeitY Order
content: Bitchat, the decentralised messaging platform founded by Twitter (now X) cofounder Jack Dorsey, has been removed from Google Play Store and Apple’s App Store following an official government order. In a post on X, Dorsey shared an official email from Apple, which read that the IT ministry (MeitY) had issued directions for the removal of the Bitchat app from the App Store under Section 69A of the IT Act. The email noted that the app allegedly included content deemed illegal in India. However, the communique did not specify what content had triggered the takedown order. Apple advised the developer to seek further details from MeitY directly. The Apple email further noted that Bitchat’s beta-testing access via TestFlight has also been blocked. However, the app would remain available on its App Store outside India. Meanwhile, Bitchat is no longer available for download via the Google Play Store as well and its website also appears to no longer be accessible in the country. It’s unclear whether this is for the same reason. Launched by Dorsey in 2025, Bitchat is an open-source messaging app that enables peer-to-peer (P2) communication through Bluetooth mesh networks without requiring internet access or centralised servers. The app does not require users to make accounts and has no central identity system either. It can be used during extreme occasions like internet outages and natural disasters, or in areas with poor network coverage. This is not the first time that Bitchat has landed in choppy regulatory waters in the country. In July this year, Dorsey had claimed the Indian government had directed GitHub to remove multiple repositories linked to Bitchat . He had shared a notification issued by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to support his claims. The I4C’s notification had raised concerns that Bitchat’s implementation of anonymous communication prevents authorities from obtaining subscriber details or communication records during active investigations. The agency also warned that the platform could be exploited to evade surveillance and bypass internet shutdowns to coordinate unlawful assemblies, protests, or criminal activities. Notably, I4C’s concerns had come amid the unrest over the NEET 2026 paper leak, when protesters were reportedly using Bitchat to communicate amid suspension of mobile internet services at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The action against Bitchat appears to be a part of Centre’s broader plan to tighten scrutiny of social media platforms. Earlier this year, MeitY had proposed amendments to the IT Rules, 2021 , which would make government advisories legally binding on online intermediaries. The draft rules also proposed requiring platforms to remove content that could be used to commit unlawful acts within three hours of receiving a court order or a reasoned government notice.
